Shinnie: Summary |website=Soccerway |publisher=Perform Group |access-date=21 July 2019}} | position = [[Attacking midfielder]] | current_club = | club_number = | youth_years1 = 2006–2008 | youth_clubs1 = [[Rangers F.C. Under-20s and Academy|Rangers]] | years1 = 2006–2011 | clubs1 = [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] | caps1 = 2 | goals1 = 0 | years2 = 2008–2009 | clubs2 = → [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] (loan) | caps2 = 20 | goals2 = 1 | years3 = 2010 | clubs3 = → [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] (loan) | caps3 = 12 | goals3 = 0 | years4 = 2011–2013 | clubs4 = [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] | caps4 = 57 | goals4 = 19 | years5 = 2013–2018 | clubs5 = [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] | caps5 = 67 | goals5 = 4 | years6 = 2016 | clubs6 = → [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] (loan) | caps6 = 3 | goals6 = 0 | years7 = 2016–2017 | clubs7 = → [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] (loan) | caps7 = 27 | goals7 = 1 | years8 = 2017–2018 | clubs8 = → [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] (loan) | caps8 = 28 | goals8 = 1 | years9 = 2018–2021 | clubs9 = [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] | caps9 = 62 | goals9 = 5 | years10 = 2020–2021 | clubs10 = → [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] (loan) | caps10 = 16 | goals10 = 2 | years11 = 2021 | clubs11 = [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] | caps11 = 13 | goals11 = 1 | years12 = 2021–2026 | clubs12 = [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] | caps12 = 133 | goals12 = 10 | national_years1 = 2007 | national_team1 = [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland U19]] | national_caps1 = 4 | national_goals1 = 0 | national_years2 = 2009–2010 | national_team2 = [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]] | national_caps2 = 3 | national_goals2 = 1 | national_years3 = 2012 | national_team3 = [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] | national_caps3 = 1 | national_goals3 = 0 | club_update = 20 May 2026 | national_team_update = | clubs13 = [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] | years13 = 2026– | caps13 = 0 | goals13 = 0 }} '''Andrew Murray Shinnie''' (born 17 July 1989) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]]. Shinnie started his professional career at [[Scottish Premier League]] side [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in 2006, but only made two league appearances in a five-year spell at the club. During his time at Rangers, he had two loan spells at [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]]: one during the [[2008–09 in Scottish football|2008–09 season]], and one in 2010, making 32 league appearances for the club. He joined [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in July 2011, and made 57 league appearances in a two-year spell at the club, featuring in the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Scottish Premier League 7|2012–13 PFA SPL Team of the Year]], before joining Birmingham City in July 2013. He spent time on loan at [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] in 2015–16, and then played on loan for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in 2016–17. After a loan spell during the 2017–18 season, Shinnie signed for Luton Town in June 2018. Shinnie played at [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] level for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] on four occasions in 2007, before making three appearances for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] side in 2009 and 2010. He made his full international debut for Scotland in November 2012, in a 2–1 win over [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]]. ==Club career== ===Rangers=== Shinnie made his first-team debut for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on 17 March 2007, coming on as a substitute for [[Dado Pršo]] in a [[Scottish Premier League]] match against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/6456633.stm |title=Rangers 3–0 Aberdeen |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 March 2007 |access-date=2 June 2018}} On the same day, he scored two goals for Rangers' under-19 team against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] under-19s.{{cite web |url=http://www.rangers.co.uk/match/match-reports/2006-07/item/2055-rangers-3-0-aberdeen |title=Rangers 3–0 Aberdeen |first=Neil |last=Smith |publisher=Rangers F.C. |date=17 March 2007 |access-date=7 July 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111020102/http://www.rangers.co.uk/match/match-reports/2006-07/item/2055-rangers-3-0-aberdeen |archive-date=11 November 2013 |df=dmy-all}} In April, he scored the first goal in the 5–0 win over rivals [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] as Rangers won the 2007 [[Scottish Youth Cup]] Final.{{cite news |url=http://www.theherald.co.uk/sport/football/display.var.1359203.0.0.php |title=Rangers U19 5–0 Celtic U19 |first=Martin |last=Greig |newspaper=The Herald |location=Glasgow |date=26 April 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070501170835/http://www.theherald.co.uk/sport/football/display.var.1359203.0.0.php |archive-date=1 May 2007}} He went on to sign a new three-year professional contract to expire in the summer of 2010.{{cite web |url=http://www.rangers.premiumtv.co.uk/page/ReserveDetail/0,,5~1067117,00.html |title=New deal for Shinnie |publisher=Rangers F.C. |date=4 July 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070707015030/http://www.rangers.premiumtv.co.uk/page/ReserveDetail/0%2C%2C5~1067117%2C00.html |archive-date=7 July 2007 |url-status=dead}} ====Dundee (loans)==== [[Scottish Football League First Division|Scottish First Division]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] signed Shinnie in November 2008 on loan for the rest of the season.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/7738286.stm |title=Shinnie moves to Dundee on loan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=19 November 2008 |access-date=28 October 2013}} On 29 November, he made his debut, coming on as a substitute in a 1–1 draw against [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]]; three months later on 21 February 2009, he scored his first senior goal in a 4–1 win over [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].{{cite news |title=Division 1: Dundee 4 Livingston 1 |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/division-1-dundee-4-livingston-1011066 |first=Anthony |last=Haggerty |newspaper=Daily Record |location=Glasgow |date=23 February 2009 |access-date=7 July 2013}} Towards the end of the season, he scored an [[own goal]] in a 2–0 defeat to [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]], and in the final game of the campaign, [[Darren Young (Scottish footballer)|Darren Young]] opened the scoring after 32 seconds against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] after the defence failed to clear Shinnie's corner; Dundee won the match 4–0.{{cite news |title=Dundee 4–0 Partick Thistle |url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/dundee-4-0-partick-thistle-1-1352644 |newspaper=The Scotsman |date=9 May 2009 |access-date=7 July 2013}} Shinnie broke his foot during pre-season, and once back to fitness, returned to Dundee in January 2010 on loan until the end of the season.{{cite news |url=http://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/Article.aspx/1582002 |title=Shinnie returns to Dundee on loan |newspaper=Press and Journal |location=Aberdeen |date=29 January 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029200958/http://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/Article.aspx/1582002 |archive-date=29 October 2013}} As in his first spell, he was a first-team regular for the duration of the loan spell.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/8709300.stm |title=Dundee sign Morton defender Dominic Shimmin |publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 May 2010 |access-date=28 October 2013}} ===Inverness Caledonian Thistle=== Released by Rangers at the end of the 2010–11 season, Shinnie signed a two-year contract with SPL club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] after impressing as a trialist in pre-season.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14032207 |title=Andrew Shinnie and Josh Meekings to join Inverness |publisher=BBC Sport |date=5 July 2011 |access-date=22 January 2017}}
{{cite web|url=http://ictfc.com/news/news-archive/75-double-capture|title=Double Capture!|website=Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|date=4 July 2011|access-date=7 November 2025|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303215639/http://ictfc.com/news/news-archive/75-double-capture|archive-date=3 March 2016|url-status=dead}} He made his debut against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] at [[Fir Park]] on 23 July.{{cite news |url=http://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/Sport/Football/ICT-crash-to-opening-day-defeat.htm |title=ICT crash to opening day defeat |newspaper=Inverness Courier |date=25 July 2011 |access-date=7 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140308132456/http://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/Sport/Football/ICT-crash-to-opening-day-defeat.htm |archive-date=8 March 2014 |url-status=dead}} Shinnie scored his first goal for Inverness in a 2–1 victory over St Mirren on 1 October, and a month later scored a hat-trick as his team beat Kilmarnock 6–3 at [[Rugby Park]].{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15504498 |title=Kilmarnock 3–6 Inverness |first=Keir |last=Murray |publisher=BBC Sport |date=5 November 2011 |access-date=7 July 2013}} On 17 December 2011, he came on as a substitute against former club Rangers at [[Ibrox Park]] and scored to make the score 1–1. It was his seventh goal of the season but Inverness lost the game 2–1.{{cite news |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/rangers-vs-inverness/237791 |title=Lafferty strike cruel on Caley |publisher=Sky Sports |date=17 December 2011 |access-date=2 June 2018}} Shinnie scored the second goal as Inverness beat [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] 3–1 in the [[2011–12 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] fourth round replay on 18 January 2012, but broke a [[metatarsal]] during the match. The injury required surgery which was expected to keep him out for the rest of the season,{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16501189 |title=Dunfermline Athletic 1–3 Inverness CT |first=Clive |last=Lindsay |publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 January 2012 |access-date=7 July 2013}}
{{cite news |url=http://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/Article.aspx/2630350 |title=Season over for Shinnie after op |first=Stephen |last=Kasiewicz |newspaper=Press and Journal |location=Aberdeen |date=8 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140308120345/http://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/Article.aspx/2630350 |archive-date=8 March 2014}} although he was fit enough to return for the last three games. He felt he had been fortunate to leave Rangers before the club's financial problems took hold.{{cite news |title=Former Rangers starlet thankful he quit the club for Inverness |url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/112171-former-rangers-starlet-thanks-his-luck-he-quit-the-club-for-inverness/ |publisher=STV Sport |date=24 July 2012 |access-date=24 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140308124736/http://sport.stv.tv/football/112171-former-rangers-starlet-thanks-his-luck-he-quit-the-club-for-inverness/|archive-date=8 March 2014|url-status=dead}} By mid-October the following season, Shinnie had scored seven goals, and manager [[Terry Butcher]] was anxious for him and teammate [[Josh Meekings]] to extend their contracts.{{cite news |title=Terry Butcher bids to tie down Caley Thistle stars |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/terry-butcher-bids-to-tie-down-1400033 |first=Alasdair |last=Fraser |newspaper=Daily Record |location=Glasgow |date=26 October 2012 |access-date=7 July 2013}} At the end of the month he scored the first goal in Inverness CT's 3–0 [[2012–13 Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] quarter-final defeat of Rangers at Ibrox.{{cite news |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/rangers-0-inverness-ct-3-end-of-ibrox-cup-dream.1351723898 |title=Rangers 0 Inverness CT 3: end of Ibrox cup dream |newspaper=The Herald |location=Glasgow |date=31 October 2012 |access-date=8 July 2013}} His form earned him his first call-up to the full [[Scotland national football team|Scotland squad]], and when he took the field in the [[exhibition game|friendly]] against [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]], he became the first Inverness CT player to be capped for Scotland at senior level. By January, he had still not signed a new contract, and was linked with fellow SPL club Aberdeen,{{cite news |title=Craig Brown set to bid for Caley Thistle star Andrew Shinnie this summer |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aberdeen-set-to-bid-for-andrew-shinnie-1548993 |newspaper=Daily Record |location=Glasgow |date=22 January 2013 |access-date=1 February 2013}} but had still not ruled out staying with Inverness CT.{{cite news |title=Inverness CT's Andrew Shinnie could stay despite Dons link |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21151306 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=22 January 2013 |access-date=1 February 2013}} Shinnie scored the opening goal in the League Cup semi-final, but opponents [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] equalised, and then won the match in a [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]].{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/scottish-league-cup/9829217/Inverness-1-Hearts-1-match-report.html |title=Inverness 1 Hearts 1: match report |first=Ewing |last=Grahame |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=26 January 2013 |access-date=8 July 2013}} Shinnie's goalscoring form dipped as the season wore on – he produced only three goals in the 17 matches after the League Cup Final, compared with thirteen from 28 before it. – but his general form earned him a place on the four-man shortlist for the 2012–13 [[SPFA Players' Player of the Year]] Award{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22276619 |title=Griffiths, Higdon, Shinnie & McGinn on SPFA shortlist |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 April 2013 |access-date=24 April 2013}} and a place in the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Scottish Premier League 7|PFA Scotland SPL Team of the Year]]{{cite web |title=PFA Scotland Teams of the Year |url=http://pfascotland.co.uk/2013/news/pfa-scotland-teams-of-the-year/ |first=Jack |last=Ross |work=PFA Scotland |date=2 May 2013 |access-date=31 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130616143205/http://pfascotland.co.uk/2013/news/pfa-scotland-teams-of-the-year/ |archive-date=16 June 2013}} ===Birmingham City=== [[File:Andrew Shinnie BCFC 2013.jpg|150px|thumb|Shinnie training with [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] in 2013 pre-season]] In April, Shinnie signed a pre-contract agreement to join English [[Football League Championship]] club [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] when his Inverness contract expired at the end of the season.{{cite news |url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/inverness/222417-birmingham-city-agree-pre-contract-deal-with-andrew-shinnie/ |title=Birmingham City agree pre-contract deal with Andrew Shinnie |publisher=STV |date=22 April 2013 |access-date=22 April 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111014408/http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/inverness/222417-birmingham-city-agree-pre-contract-deal-with-andrew-shinnie/ |archive-date=11 November 2013 |url-status=dead}} He stated the move was "a difficult decision", but that "a three-year deal in a good league like the Championship was the right decision." and that he hoped the move would help him push for a place in the national team.{{cite news |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11694/8670543/Birmingham-new-boy-Andrew-Shinnie-admits-it-was-tough-to-leave-Inverness |title=Birmingham new boy Andrew Shinnie admits it was tough to leave Inverness |publisher=Sky Sports |date=27 April 2013 |access-date=3 May 2013 |first=Pete |last=O'Rourke}} Shinnie made his Birmingham debut in a 1–0 defeat to [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] on the opening day of the season. He scored his first goal in the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] against [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]], when he "lashed home [[Chris Burke (footballer)|Chris Burke]]'s fizzing cross"; Birmingham progressed to the third round on penalties.{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/league-cup/10269825/Yeovil-Town-3-Birmingham-City-3-pens-2-3-match-report.html |title=Yeovil Town 3 Birmingham City 3 (pens 2–3): match report |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |date=27 August 2013 |access-date=4 September 2013}} He should have scored at [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] in September, when he "blazed his shot over the crossbar" after Birmingham broke at pace,{{cite news |url=http://www.kilburntimes.co.uk/sport/football/queens-park-rangers/austin_guides_qpr_to_victory_over_birmingham_1_2511376 |title=Austin guides QPR to victory over Birmingham |first=Ian |last=Cooper |newspaper=Kilburn Times |date=14 September 2013 |access-date=22 January 2016}} and he spent four games out of the league side, during which time he worked in the gym to improve his physical strength and in training on sharpness. He returned to orchestrate a 4–0 win against [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] when manager [[Lee Clark (footballer)|Lee Clark]]'s change of formation allowed him to play in his preferred [[playmaker]] role,{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-andrew-shinnies-spell-6141007 |title=Andrew Shinnie's spell on the sidelines was 'a good thing' |first=Colin |last=Tattum |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=5 October 2013 |access-date=25 January 2016}}{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-boss-lee-clark-6123559 |title=Lee Clark: If Andrew Shinnie keeps playing like that the goals will come as well |first=Colin |last=Tattum |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=2 October 2013 |access-date=22 January 2016}} and his first league goal opened the scoring in a 2–0 win at [[AFC Bournemouth]] on 14 December.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25275171 |title=Bournemouth 0 Birmingham 2 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 December 2013 |access-date=25 January 2016}} He was regularly involved on matchdays for a time, but it was often as a substitute or in an unaccustomed wide position,{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-andrew-shinnie-keen-7545742 |title=Andrew Shinnie keen to be more than just handy Andy for Blues |first=Colin |last=Tattum |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=14 August 2014 |access-date=25 January 2016}} and he was out of the side entirely between mid-January and March 2014. He returned with a good performance in a 3–3 draw at [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]],{{cite news |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11694/9210280/sky-bet-championship-birmingham-earn-3-3-draw-with-burnley |title=Sky Bet Championship: Birmingham earn 3-3 draw with Burnley |publisher=Sky Sports |date=12 March 2014 |access-date=2 June 2018}} and scored a headed goal in a 3–2 win away at fellow relegation candidates Millwall,{{cite news |url=http://www.london24.com/sport/football/clubs/millwall/birmingham_deal_hammer_blow_to_millwall_s_survival_hopes_1_3485973 |title=Birmingham deal hammer blow to Millwall's survival hopes |first=Tom |last=Moore |website=London24 |date=25 March 2014 |access-date=25 January 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201040916/http://www.london24.com/sport/football/clubs/millwall/birmingham_deal_hammer_blow_to_millwall_s_survival_hopes_1_3485973 |archive-date=1 February 2016}} but was substituted early in the next match when Clark wanted to field an extra striker.{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/match-reports/birmingham-city-2-bournemouth-4-6896992 |title=Birmingham City 2 Bournemouth 4 – player ratings and match stats |first=Gary |last=Young |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=31 March 2014 |access-date=25 January 2016}} He was an unused substitute in the final match of the season, as Birmingham came back from 2–0 down at [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] to avoid relegation on [[goal difference]] via a stoppage-time equaliser and other results going in their favour.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27167525 |title=Bolton 2 Birmingham 2 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 May 2014 |access-date=25 January 2016}} Shinnie started the opening match of the [[2014–15 Birmingham City F.C. season|2014–15 season]], but was omitted from the next two, and then injured his back playing for the under-21 side.{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-boss-lee-clark-7636391 |title=Birmingham City boss Lee Clark wants to see consistency from his side |first=Colin |last=Tattum |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=19 August 2014 |access-date=25 January 2016}} His next first-team appearance was at [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] on 21 October when he was recalled to the squad by the [[caretaker manager]]s the day after Clark was sacked; he came on in the 80th minute and came close to scoring an equaliser when his shot from {{convert|20|yards}} struck the underside of the crossbar but failed to cross the line.{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/match-reports/blackburn-1-birmingham-city-0-7975944 |title=Blackburn 1 Birmingham City 0 |first=Colin |last=Tattum |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=21 October 2014 |access-date=25 January 2016}} Incoming manager [[Gary Rowett]] used Shinnie as the creative player in his preferred [[formation (association football)#4–2–3–1|4–2–3–1 formation]], and he thrived in the role.{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-andy-shinnie-having-8180119 |title=Birmingham City: Andy Shinnie having more influence under Gary Rowett – the stats prove it |first=Brian |last=Dick |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=26 November 2014 |access-date=25 January 2016}} By December, the ''[[Birmingham Mail]]''{{'s}} reporter thought he was "enjoying the finest spell of his Birmingham career", and a goal in a 6–1 defeat of [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] was a deserved reward for what Rowett called "fantastic" work-rate and build-up play.{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-goal-boost-andrew-8291940 |title=Birmingham City: Goal will boost Andrew Shinnie's confidence, says Gary Rowett |first=Brian |last=Dick |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=16 December 2014 |access-date=25 January 2016}} In March 2015, he scored the winner against Clark's new club, [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]],{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-gary-rowett-delighted-8773605 |title=Birmingham City: Gary Rowett delighted for goalscorer Andy Shinnie |first=Brian |last=Dick |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=4 March 2015 |access-date=25 January 2016}} but then lost his regular place to loanee [[Diego Fabbrini]].{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-end-of-season-reports---9252857 |title=Birmingham City end-of-season reports – we rate the midfielders |first=Brian |last=Dick |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=14 May 2015 |access-date=25 January 2016}} Shinnie signed a two-year contract extension in the 2015 close season,{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33725970 |title=Birmingham City: Jon Toral signs on loan from Arsenal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=30 July 2016 |access-date=25 January 2016}} but lost his first-choice playmaker role to loanee [[Jon Toral]], whose goalscoring – and the fact that he was part of a winning side – made him hard to leave out.{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-gary-rowett-considering-10074686 |title=Birmingham City: Gary Rowett considering Andy Shinnie recall |first=Brian |last=Dick |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=17 September 2015 |access-date=25 January 2016}} ====Loans==== Shinnie joined fellow Championship club [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] on 27 January 2016 on loan until the end of the season.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35421530 |title=Andrew Shinnie: Rotherham United sign Birmingham City man |publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 January 2016 |access-date=27 January 2016}} He made his debut three days later, as a second-half substitute with his side 2–1 down at home to [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]]; the match finished as a 4–1 defeat. He fell out of favour under [[Neil Warnock]], who replaced [[Neil Redfearn]] as manager shortly after Shinnie's arrival, and made only three appearances during his loan spell.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35541314 |title=Neil Warnock named Rotherham manager until end of season |publisher=BBC Sport |date=11 February 2016 |access-date=28 July 2016}} Despite performing well in 2016 pre-season, Shinnie remained behind Diego Fabbrini as Birmingham's playmaker of choice, and on 17 August, he signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on loan for the season.{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/gary-rowett-deal-virtually-agreed-11751361 |title=Gary Rowett: Deal virtually agreed with club for Birmingham City midfielder |first=Brian |last=Dick |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=15 August 2015 |access-date=17 August 2016}}{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/6731 |title=Andrew Shinnie joins Hibernian on loan |publisher=Hibernian F.C. |date=17 August 2016 |access-date=17 August 2016}} He made his debut in Hibs' next match, coming on after 69 minutes with his side 2–0 ahead against St Mirren. '''Ryan Flynn''' (born 4 September 1988) is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] [[Association footballer|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]]. Born in [[Edinburgh]], he started his career with [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] before spells at [[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]], [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] and [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]]. He has also represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19 level]].

==Career==

===Liverpool===
Flynn began his career as a junior player with [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], but signed for Liverpool in 2005 for £50,000.<ref name="liverpool signing">{{cite web|url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/team/squad/flynn/|publisher=Liverpool F.C.|title=Ryan Flynn|date=30 June 2009|access-date=15 July 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091129062641/http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/team/squad/flynn/|archive-date=29 November 2009}}</ref> Flynn helped Liverpool win successive FA Youth Cup victories in the 2005–06 and 2006–07 seasons, scoring the winner in front of the Kop against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the 2006 final and scoring in the penalty shoot-out at Old Trafford (Stretford End) against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the 2007 final.<ref name="liverpool echo" /> In his third season at the club, he helped them win the Northern Premier Reserve League Title, in the 2007–08 season.<ref name="liverpool echo" /> In November 2007, Flynn joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Hereford United F.C.|Hereford United]] on a month's loan, although failed to make an appearance.<ref>{{Cite news |date=22 November 2007 |title=Hereford net Liverpool midfielder |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/h/hereford_united/7108176.stm |access-date=7 May 2025 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> Flynn was loaned to [[Conference National]] club [[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]] for the latter part of the 2008–09 season.<ref name="liverpool echo" /> In all, Flynn scored four goals in 25 league appearances for Wrexham.<ref name="liverpool echo">{{cite web|url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2009/06/30/liverpool-fc-latest-ryan-flynn-set-for-another-season-on-loan-100252-24025324|publisher=Liverpool Echo|title=Ryan Flynn set for another season on loan|date=30 June 2009|access-date=15 July 2011}}</ref>

===Falkirk===
Flynn was then loaned back to his first club, Falkirk, for the [[2009–10 Falkirk F.C. season|2009–10 season]].<ref name="liverpool echo" /> He made his Falkirk début in a [[UEFA Europa League]] tie against [[FC Vaduz]], and Flynn scored the only goal of the game, becoming the first Falkirk player to score a goal in European competition.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8152287.stm |title=Falkirk 1–0 Vaduz |publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 June 2009|access-date=15 July 2011}}</ref> In mid September it was announced that his move had been made permanent and he signed a three-year contract with Falkirk.<ref name = "flynn award"/> Flynn won the [[Scottish Premier League]] award for Young Player of the Month for March 2010, having scored six goals in 33 games for Falkirk. He also won the Young Player of the Round award in the second round of the [[2010–11 Scottish League Cup]], in which he scored the only goal to put Falkirk through against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] In the third round of the same cup he was part of the Falkirk team that were voted 'Team of the round', a game in which he scored the third goal against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] and which ended up 4–3 to Falkirk.<ref name = "flynn award"/>

===Sheffield United===
On 14 July 2011, Flynn signed for [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] for an undisclosed fee on a three-year deal.<ref name="blades deal">{{cite web |url=http://www.sufc.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10418~2392890,00.html|publisher=Sheffield United F.C.|title=United capture mighty Flynn|date=14 July 2011|access-date=14 July 2011|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719022439/http://www.sufc.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10418~2392890,00.html|archive-date=19 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=5417&Itemid=320|title=Flynn heads for Sheffield United|website=Falkirk F.C.|date=14 July 2011|access-date=18 June 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120414233157/http://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=5417&Itemid=320|archive-date=14 April 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He made his competitive club début on the first day of the 2011–12 season, starting the [[Football League]] match against [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Oldham 0–2 Sheffield Utd |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14352031 |publisher=BBC |date=6 August 2011 |access-date=6 August 2011 }}</ref> During his first season at [[Bramall Lane]] Flynn established himself as first team player despite competing with the likes of Republic of Ireland International [[Stephen Quinn]] for a place in the starting eleven. He finished the campaign having made thirty five appearances and scored three goals. This campaign ended with United finishing 3rd in League One and making the Play Off final. Flynn started in this game as United lost on penalties to Huddersfield at Wembley.

In season 2012–13 Flynn appeared 44 times for the Blades scoring three goals as the side again made the play offs in League One. In 2013–14 Sheffield United embarked on a memorable FA Cup campaign which culminated in them reaching the Semi-Final at Wembley in which they lost 5–3 to Hull City. Flynn starred for the side throughout the campaign, scoring the winning goal against Premier League side Aston Villa at Villa Park and also scoring as they beat Championship side Charlton.

In May 2014, Flynn signed an extension to his contract for a further two-year with the option of a third year.<ref name="new deal">{{Cite web|title=Flynn signs new Blades deal|url=http://www.sufc.co.uk/news/article/20140502-flynn-signs-1523736.aspx|publisher=Sheffield United F.C.|date=2 May 2014|access-date=2 May 2014}}</ref>

In 2014–15 Flynn and Sheffield United went on another famous cup run, this time making the semi-final of the League Cup. They beat West Ham at Upton Park as well as Southampton at Bramall Lane en route to the Semi Final where they met Spurs and lost narrowly 3–2 on aggregate. Flynn showed his versatility by starting both games against Spurs at right back and performing impressively. The season ended once more with United making the League One Play Offs only to lose to Swindon Town 7–6 on aggregate.

===Oldham Athletic===
On 13 July 2016, Flynn signed a two-year deal with [[EFL League One|League One]] side Oldham Athletic.<ref>{{cite news|title=SIGNING: Flynn Signs For Oldham Athletic|url=http://www.oldhamathletic.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/signing-flynn-signs-for-oldham-athletic-3184260.aspx|publisher=Oldham Athletic|date=13 July 2016|access-date=14 July 2016}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Oldham in a 2–1 [[EFL Cup]] win against [[Wigan Athletic]] on 9 August 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36949056 |title=Oldham 2-1 Wigan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 August 2016 |access-date=9 August 2016}}</ref> He was released by Oldham in January 2018.

===St Mirren===
On 15 January 2018, Flynn joined [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on a two-and-a-half-year deal and helped the club secure the Scottish Championship title and promotion in May 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/1495-ryan-flynn-joins-the-buddies|title=Ryan Flynn joins The Buddies|work=stmirren.com|date=15 January 2018|access-date=15 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42691644 |title=Ryan Flynn: St Mirren sign former Liverpool and Falkirk midfielder |publisher=BBC Sport |date=15 January 2018 |access-date=15 January 2018}}</ref> Season 2018-19 saw St Mirren, with Flynn as a key player, stay in the Premier League thanks to a memorable end of season run and win over Dundee United in the Premiership Play off.

Flynn suffered cruciate ligament damage on 5 February 2020 in a match against [[Hamilton Academicals F.C.|Hamilton Academicals]], which effectively ended his season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51417219 |title=Ryan Flynn: St Mirren player suffers crucial ligament damage |publisher=BBC Sport |date=7 February 2020 |access-date=10 February 2020}}</ref>

Flynn signed a new one-year contract in June 2020, after becoming an integral part of the Saints squad and a firm fans favourite.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52896832 |title=St Mirren: Ryan Flynn signs new one-year contract |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 June 2020 |access-date=22 June 2020}}</ref> Flynn's contract was extended for a further year in 2021 after a successful return to full fitness in November 2020. In November 2021, Flynn played his 100th game for St Mirren and was praised by Manager Jim Goodwin for being a real model professional who could play in a number of positions and always perform.

Following Goodwin's departure, Flynn has become a key part of Stephen Robinson's squad. The pair worked together at Oldham and has led to Flynn taking the first steps towards coaching while playing his part for a St Mirren side which secured a top 6 place in 2022–23. Flynn's versatility and experience remained a key component in the St Mirren squad.

===Arbroath===
On 30 August 2024, Flynn signed with [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] in the third-tier [[Scottish League One]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Arbroath|url=https://arbroathfc.co.uk/transfer-deadline-day-action-at-arbroath/|title=Transfer deadline day action at Arbroath|date=30 August 2024|access-date=26 December 2024}}</ref>

'''Ryan Dow''' (born 7 June 1991) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] or [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].

A product of the [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] youth system, he turned professional in 2007. After making his first team debut in 2011, he went on to become a first team regular after a spell on loan to [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]]. He left Dundee United in the 2016 close season and signed for [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in September. Dow moved to Peterhead during the 2018–19 season, initially on loan. In May 2019 he signed for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

==Early life==
Ryan Dow was born in [[Dundee]] on 7 June 1991. He attended [[Harris Academy]] in the city, and was part of the school football team that won the Scottish Schools' Shield in 2005. having previously been attached to [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] as a youth player, Dow joined [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in 2005, going on to sign a professional contract in June 2007. He also went on and won the Scottish cup with Dundee United in 2010.<ref name=DUFC>{{cite web|title=First team - Ryan Dow|url=http://dufc.co/the-teams/first-team/6114/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150323045308/http://dufc.co/the-teams/first-team/6114/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=23 March 2015|publisher=Dundee United F.C.|access-date=20 January 2016}}</ref>

==Playing career==

===Dundee United===
Dow's first involvement with the Dundee United first team came in July 2007, when he appeared as a substitute in a pre-season friendly against [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrie United]]. Over the next three years he established himself in the Dundee United youth and reserve sides, and was top scorer for the under-19 team in season 2008–09.<ref name=DUFC /> It was announced in July 2009 that Dow would be joining [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] on loan,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/index.asp?tm=2&nID=3237&cd=2009&cd1=7 |title=KEEPER SIGNS PRE CONTRACT |publisher=[[Dundee United F.C.]] |access-date=23 June 2014 |date=6 July 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140623202135/http://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/index.asp?tm=2&nID=3237&cd=2009&cd1=7 |archive-date=23 June 2014 |url-status=unfit }}</ref> but the move was never completed.

Dow made his competitive debut for the Dundee United first team on 1 May 2010, at home to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]. After coming on as an early substitute, he set up United's goal in the 2–1 defeat.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dundee United 1 - 2 Rangers|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/8653025.stm|work=BBC Sport|last=Lindsay|first=Clive|date=1 May 2010|access-date=23 June 2014}}</ref> Dow was named man of the match and, shortly afterwards, he signed a contract extension until 2012.<ref>{{cite news|title=Tannadice duo extend Dundee United contracts|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/d/dundee_utd/8692364.stm|work=BBC Sport|date=19 May 2010|access-date=23 June 2014}}</ref>

Dow was named in 12 matchday squads during the 2010–11 season, but made only one substitute appearance, against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in November 2010.<ref name=DUFC /> He was loaned out to Forfar Athletic in March 2011 for the remainder of the season, to gain experience.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/Article.aspx/2178403 |title=Dow goes straight in for Forfar |publisher=Press and Journal |access-date=23 June 2014 |date=15 March 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203001233/http://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/Article.aspx/2178403 |archive-date=3 December 2013 |url-status=unfit }}</ref> He made twelve appearances for the [[Scottish Football League Second Division|Second Division]] club, scoring three goals and helping them reach the promotion play-offs.<ref>{{Soccerbase season|48437|2010|name=Ryan Dow|access-date=23 June 2014}}</ref> Dow later described his time at Forfar as "a great experience... It does toughen you up when you go down to the lower leagues".<ref name=Courier>{{cite news|last1=Robertson|first1=Neil|title=Dundee United v Inverness: Patient Ryan Dow aiming to cement his place|url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-united/dundee-united-v-inverness-patient-ryan-dow-aiming-to-cement-his-place-1.119342|access-date=20 January 2016|work=The Courier|date=10 August 2013|location=Dundee}}</ref>

Over the next two seasons, Dow began to feature more regularly in the Dundee United squad. He scored his first goal for the club on 20 September 2011, when he opened the scoring in a [[Scottish League Cup]] tie against Airdrie United.<ref>{{cite news|title=Terrors made to work at Airdrie|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/match_report/0,19764,11065_3448747,00.html|access-date=23 September 2011|work=Sky Sports|publisher=BSkyB|date=20 September 2011}}</ref> He signed an extended contract in October 2011, keeping him at Dundee United until 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15389334|title=Ryan Dow agrees new deal at Dundee United|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=20 October 2011|access-date=20 October 2011}}</ref> His first league goal came on 11 May 2013, in a 2–1 win over [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Inverness Caledonian Thistle 1 - 2 Dundee United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22409627|work=BBC Sport|last=Spence|first=Jim|date=11 May 2013|access-date=23 June 2014}}</ref>

Dow began to play more regularly after [[Jackie McNamara]] became Dundee United manager in 2013. He was selected to start in the first match of the [[2013–14 Dundee United F.C. season|2013–14 season]], ahead of more established players like [[Gary Mackay-Steven]].<ref name=Courier /> As the season progressed, Dow was often selected in the middle of a front three formation, despite strong competition for the attacking positions in the team.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Gordon|first1=Moira|title=Tide has turned for Dundee United's Ryan Dow|url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/teams/dundee-united/tide-has-turned-for-dundee-united-s-ryan-dow-1-3333868|access-date=20 January 2016|work=The Scotsman|date=9 March 2014|location=Edinburgh}}</ref> He later had an extended run in the first team and scored his first goal of the season, in a 3–1 win over [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on 21 February 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Scottish Premiership: Dundee United 3-1 Motherwell|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26183919|work=BBC Sport|last=Southwick|first=Andrew|date=21 February 2014|access-date=23 June 2014}}</ref> His second goal came on 26 March 2014, as Dundee United beat Inverness 2–1.<ref>{{cite news|title=Scottish Premiership: Dundee United 2-1 Inverness Caledonian Thistle|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26641362|work=BBC Sport|last=Southwick|first=Andrew|date=26 March 2014|access-date=23 June 2014}}</ref> Then, on 26 April 2014, Dow scored his third goal of the season in a 5–1 win over Motherwell.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dundee United 5 - 1 Motherwell|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27084806|work=BBC Sport|last=Sutherland|first=Jonathan|date=26 April 2014|access-date=23 June 2014}}</ref> On 13 May 2014, Dow signed a new contract until 2016, ending three months of negotiations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/index.asp?tm=2&nID=4815&cd=2014&cd1=5 |title=CONTRACT EXTENSIONS FOR DOW AND McCALLUM |publisher=[[Dundee United F.C.]] |access-date=23 June 2014 |date=13 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140623211214/http://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/index.asp?tm=2&nID=4815&cd=2014&cd1=5 |archive-date=23 June 2014 |url-status=unfit }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Ryan Dow opens talks over new deal at Dundee United|url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-united/ryan-dow-opens-talks-over-new-deal-at-dundee-united-1.239416|publisher=The Courier|date=25 February 2014|access-date=23 June 2014}}</ref> A few days after signing his new deal, Dow started in the [[2014 Scottish Cup Final|Scottish Cup Final]], as Dundee United lost 2–0 to [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Scottish Cup Final: St Johnstone 2 - 0 Dundee United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27354162|work=BBC Sport|last=Wilson|first=Richard|date=17 May 2014|access-date=23 June 2014}}</ref>

Dow was released by Dundee United at the end of the 2015–16 season, with the club having been relegated to the [[Scottish Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee United confirm eight released|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/167078/dundee-united-confirm-eight-released/|publisher=The Courier|last=Nicolson|first=Eric|date=4 May 2016|access-date=10 September 2016}}</ref>

===Ross County===
Dow signed for [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on 9 September 2016, having recovered from injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news/archive/ryan-dow-joins-ross-county-football-club/ |title=Ryan Dow signs on at Ross County until the end of the season |publisher=Ross County FC |date=9 September 2016 |access-date=9 September 2016}}</ref> He extended his contract with Ross County for a further two years in May 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/scotland/39852643 |title=Ross County: Ryan Dow agrees two-year contract extension |first=Martin |last=Dowden |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=9 May 2017 |access-date=9 May 2017}}</ref> Dow left [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on 3 January 2019, by mutual consent having made 54 appearances for the club scoring only 1 goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news/archive/ryan-dow-departs-dingwall/|title=Ryan Dow Departs the Club|publisher=Ross County |date=3 January 2019 |access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref>

===Peterhead===
On 14 September 2018, Dow joined [[Scottish League Two]] side [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] on loan until January 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/1562983/peterhead-confirm-loan-signing-of-ross-county-forward-ryan-dow/|title=Peterhead confirm loan signing of Ross County forward Ryan Dow|publisher=Press and Journal|date=14 September 2018|access-date=14 September 2018}}</ref> On 3 January 2019, he left Ross County and joined Peterhead on a free transfer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.peterheadfc.com/news/item/2432-ryan-returns-after-ross-county-release|title=Ryan returns after Ross County release|publisher=Peterhead FC|date=3 January 2019|access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref>

===Dunfermline Athletic===
Following a successful spell with Peterhead, it was announced on 14 May 2019, that Dow had signed a one-year deal with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Dow_is_a_Par&ID=11236 |title=Dow is a Par |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=14 May 2019 |access-date=14 May 2019}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 3–2 win away to [[Scottish Premiership]] side St Mirren in the group stage of the League Cup.<ref>{{cite web|title=St Mirren 2–3 Dunfermline|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48969502|work=BBC Sport|last=Duncan|first=Thomas|date=14 July 2019|access-date=30 July 2019}}</ref> Dow was released at the end of the 2021/2022 season following the team's relegation to [[Scottish League One|League One]].

'''Gavin Christopher Reilly''' (born 10 May 1993) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (football)|striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].

==Career==
===Queen of the South (first spell)===
Reilly arrived through the youth ranks of [[Dumfries]] club [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]], signing a professional contract before the start of the [[2010-11 in Scottish football|2010–11]] season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://live.qosstats.info/live/new_newsview.aspx?newsid=65|title=Qosstats.info}}{{Dead link|date=December 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He made his competitive first-team debut on 31 July 2010, in a 5–1 [[Scottish League Cup]] first round win versus [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] as an 83rd-minute substitute for [[Derek Holmes]]. Reilly marked the occasion by scoring the team's fifth and final goal of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://live.qosstats.info/live/new_report.aspx?fixtureid=134|title=Qosstats.info}}{{dead link|date=May 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Reilly's league debut was as an 86th minute substitute in the season's opening 1–0 away defeat away to [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://live.qosstats.info/live/new_report.aspx?fixtureid=135|title=Qosstats.info}}{{Dead link|date=December 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Reilly scored 15 goals in 22 starts during the [[2012–13 in Scottish football|2012–13]] season and then scored 12 goals in 19 league starts in the [[2013–14 in Scottish football|2013–14]] season.{{citation needed|date=June 2015}} In August 2014, he went on trial with English Championship club [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/queen-south-hoping-hold-top-4936007 | title=Queen of the South hoping to hold on to top players for promotion play-off push |work=Daily Record|location=Scotland  | date=8 January 2015 | access-date=23 June 2015}}</ref>

===Heart of Midlothian===
On 23 June 2015, it was announced that Reilly had signed a three-year contract with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], with an undisclosed development fee being paid to Queen of the South.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11790/9893246/hearts-sign-queen-of-the-south-striker-gavin-reilly | title=Hearts sign Queen of the South striker Gavin Reilly | publisher=skysports.com | date=23 June 2015 | access-date=23 June 2015}}</ref> The announcement stated that Reilly had scored 44 first team goals in over 140 games, including over 80 starting appearances since his debut as a 17-year-old.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.qosfc.com/new_newsview.aspx?newsid=2837|title=QosFC: Gavin is a Jambo}}</ref><ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33240530 Hearts: Striker Gavin Reilly agrees three-year deal], BBC Sport</ref> He scored his first goal for Hearts on 12 August 2015, in a 6–0 win versus [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] from the penalty spot.

In June 2016, Reilly joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on a year-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Gavin_Reilly_joins_Dunfermline&ID=9333 |title=Gavin Reilly joins Dunfermline |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=13 June 2016 |access-date=13 June 2016}}</ref> He had previously worked with Dunfermline manager [[Allan Johnston]] at Queen of the South, where he helped the club win the [[Scottish Football League Second Division|Scottish Second Division]] and also the [[2013 Scottish Challenge Cup Final]] versus [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in the [[2012–13 in Scottish football|2012–13 season]]. Reilly's first appearance for the ''Pars'' was in a 3–0 victory at [[East End Park]] in the Scottish League Cup<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dafc.co.uk/fixture.php?SID=First%20Team&D=2016-07-19&ID=957 |title=Dunfermline 3 Arbroath 0 |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=19 July 2016 |access-date=23 August 2016}}</ref> and his first goal arrived in a 2–1 defeat away to [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] at [[Easter Road]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36994675 |title=Hibernian 2 – 1 Dunfermline |first=Brian |last=McLaughlin |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 August 2016 |access-date=23 August 2016}}</ref> After the arrival of his former ''Queens'' strike-partner [[Nicky Clark]] from [[Bury F.C.|Bury]] at the end of August 2016, Reilly's remaining minutes on the pitch were restricted to second-half substitute appearances and he ended his season with the club, having scored 2 goals in 28 appearances.

===St Mirren===
Reilly signed a one-year deal with Scottish Championship club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on 12 June 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/925-st-mirren-sign-gavin-reilly |title=St Mirren sign Gavin Reilly |publisher=St Mirren |date=13 June 2017 |access-date=13 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171210071613/https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/925-st-mirren-sign-gavin-reilly |archive-date=10 December 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://stv.tv/sport/football/1391034-st-mirren-sign-striker-gavin-reilly-on-one-year-deal/ |title=St Mirren sign striker Gavin Reilly on one-year deal |first=Ronnie |last=Charters |work=STV News |publisher=STV |date=12 June 2017 |access-date=12 June 2017 |archive-date=22 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170822015426/https://stv.tv/sport/football/1391034-st-mirren-sign-striker-gavin-reilly-on-one-year-deal/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He scored 22 goals in 44 games for Saints, as he helped fire them to the Scottish Championship title. Reilly left St Mirren at the end of the season when new manager [[Alan Stubbs]] opted to withdraw the offer of a new contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gavin Reilly stunned by St Mirren exit as Alan Stubbs rips up striker's contract offer|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/gavin-reilly-stunned-st-mirren-12739281|website=dailyrecord.co.uk|last=Parks|first=Gordon|date=19 June 2018|access-date=6 January 2021}}</ref>

===Bristol Rovers===
In July 2018, Reilly departed the ''Buddies'' and signed for [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]] on a free transfer.<ref name = "bristol rovers">{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44698668 | title=Gavin Reilly: Bristol Rovers sign former St Mirren striker |work=BBC Sport|date=3 July 2018 | access-date=3 July 2018}}</ref> On 22 September 2018, he scored his first league goal for the ''Pirates'' in the 7th minute at home to [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] in a 3–1 win.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bristol Rovers 3–1 Coventry City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45529619|website=BBC Sport|date=22 September 2018}}</ref> In 2018–19 he featured in 35 competitive first team games, of which he started 16 in the league and was brought on as substitute 14 times. He was substituted in 13 of those league games that he started. From the 35 games in which he played he scored 4 goals.<ref name=way>[https://int.soccerway.com/players/gavin-reilly/137597/ Gavin Reilly on Soccerway]</ref>

Reilly was not offered a new deal with the League One club at the end of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Retained List Announced |url=https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/2020/june/bristol-rovers-retained-list/ |access-date=4 August 2020 |website=www.bristolrovers.co.uk |date=15 June 2020 |archive-date=15 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200615123639/https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/2020/june/bristol-rovers-retained-list/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

====Cheltenham Town (loan)====
On 1 August 2019, Reilly joined English [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]] on loan for the first half of the 2019-20 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/49192735|title=Gavin Reilly: Cheltenham Town sign Bristol Rovers striker on loan|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 August 2019}}</ref>

===Carlisle United===
On 4 August 2020, Reilly signed a one-year contract with [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]] following his release from Bristol Rovers.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.carlisleunited.co.uk/news/2020/august/contract-gretna-born-forward-joins-united/|title= CONTRACT: Gretna-born forward joins United|website=www.carlisleunited.co.uk|date=4 August 2020|access-date=4 August 2020}}</ref>
On 5 January 2021, Reilly left [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]] via mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|title=CLUB: Striker moves on|url=https://www.carlisleunited.co.uk/news/2021/january/club-striker-moves-on/|website=carlisleunited.co.uk|last=Hall|first=Andy|date=5 January 2021}}</ref><ref name=livi>{{cite web|title=Striker Gavin Reilly joins Livingston after Carlisle United departure|url=https://www.newsandstar.co.uk/sport/18986913.striker-gavin-reilly-leaves-carlisle-united-mutual-consent/|website=newsandstar.co.uk|last=Colman|first=Jon|date=5 January 2021}}</ref>

===Livingston===
On 5 January 2021, Reilly signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on an 18-month contract.<ref name=livi/><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55550437 |title=Livingston sign striker Gavin Reilly from Carlisle United |publisher=BBC Sport |date=5 January 2021}}</ref>

On 30 August 2021, Reilly was sent on loan to [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] for the entire [[2021–22 Scottish Championship|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/gavin-reilly-goes-on-loan-to-morton/|title=Gavin Reilly goes on-loan to Morton|website=livingstonf.co.uk|date=30 August 2021|accessdate=31 August 2021}}</ref>

=== Queen of the South (second spell) ===
On 24 May 2022, Reilly returned to [[Dumfries]] club [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] on a two-year contract, despite the ''Doonhamers'' relegation to [[Scottish League One]] at the end of the [[2021-22 in Scottish football|2021-22]] season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=QosFC: He's Back............... |url=http://www.qosfc.com/news-5772 |access-date=2022-05-24 |website=www.qosfc.com}}</ref>

=== Stenhousemuir (loan) ===
On 23 February 2023, Reilly was loaned out to [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.qosfc.com/news-6025 | title=QosFC: Reilly is a Warrior }}</ref>

=== Arbroath ===
On 6 May 2024, Reilly signed a pre-contract with [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on a two-year deal, having decided to play part-time whilst taking up an apprenticeship outside the game.<ref>{{Cite web | title=QosFC: Gavin Reilly | url=https://www.qosfc.com/news-6386 | access-date=2026-09-25 | website=www.qosfc.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | title=Arbroath FC (@ArbroathFC) / X | url=https://twitter.com/arbroathfc | access-date=2026-09-25 | website=twitter.com}}</ref>

'''Darren Jamieson''' (born 15 February 1991) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]], who plays as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Stenhous}} club [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=TRANSFER NEWS|url=https://twitter.com/keltyheartsfc/status/1280239643452223490|access-date=2020-07-07|via=Twitter}}</ref>

Jamieson has previously played for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], [[Bo'ness United F.C.|Bo'ness United]], [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] and [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]].

==Early life==
Jamieson grew up in Polbeth, West Lothian and attended West Calder high school. He played in goal from a young age with Murieston United alongside pros like [[Danny Wilson (footballer, born 1991)|Danny Wilson]] and [[Rhys McCabe]]. Jamieson was then scouted by [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] where he played for a few years before leaving for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

==Career==

===Livingston===
A product of Livingston's youth system, Jamieson made his debut for the first-team on 27 April 2010, in a 2–0 home win over [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]] in the [[Scottish Third Division]].<ref>{{cite web | url= https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_div_1/8645434.stm | title=Livingston 2-0 Albion Rovers match report | publisher=BBC | date=27 April 2010 | access-date=28 April 2013}}</ref> His next appearance came the following season on 7 May 2011, in a 3–1 away win against [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] in the [[Scottish Second Division]].<ref name="DJ10">{{Soccerbase season|49025|2010|accessdate=28 May 2013}}</ref> Over the next couple of seasons, he was mainly utilised as reserve keeper in the first-team. He made three consecutive [[Scottish First Division]] appearances towards the end of season 2012–13, keeping two clean sheets in those three matches. Jamieson cemented his place as the number 1 goalkeeper at Livingston and in his first season as #1 saved five penalties.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/west-lothian-football-darren-jamieson-3291953|title=Darren Jamieson saves day for Livingston with third penalty stop in four games|date=27 March 2014}}</ref> He was awarded both supporters young player and play of the year at the end of the season.

After [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] goalkeeper [[Liam Kelly (footballer, born 1996)|Liam Kelly]] signed on loan with Livingston at the beginning of the [[2016–17 in Scottish football|2016–17 season]], Jamieson was sent on loan to [[Scottish Junior Football East Region Super League]] side [[Bo'ness United F.C.|Bo'ness United]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://livingstonfc.co.uk/dj-lends-boness-hand/ |title=DJ lends Bo'ness a hand |work=livingstonfc.co.uk |publisher=Livingston FC |date=10 August 2016 |accessdate=29 August 2016}}</ref>

=== Hamilton Academical ===
Jamieson was released by Livingston on 31 August 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1961&newsID=16471&newsCategoryID=1 |title=Completed Transfers - Deadline Day August 2016 |publisher=Scottish FA |date=31 August 2016 |accessdate=31 August 2016}}</ref> Livingston said that he had been released in order to join [[Scottish Premiership|Premiership]] club [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37238697 |title=Darren Jamieson: Goalkeeper released to join Hamilton, say Livingston |publisher=BBC Sport  |date=1 September 2016 |accessdate=1 September 2016}}</ref> but he was not a Hamilton squad member by 9 September.<ref>{{cite web|title=Squad and Squad Number Update|date=9 September 2016|url=http://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/squad-and-squad-number-update/|publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C.|access-date=11 September 2016|archive-date=24 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924122652/http://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/squad-and-squad-number-update/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He finally signed for Hamilton later that month, after a spell with Bo'ness.<ref>{{cite web|title=Goalie Signs|url=http://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/goalie-signs/|publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C|date=25 September 2017|access-date=26 September 2016|archive-date=25 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200625081846/https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/goalie-signs/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Jamieson was one of seven first-team players released by Hamilton at the end of the 2017–18 season,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/teams/hamilton-accies/hamilton-accies-announce-departure-of-seven-first-team-players-1-4739307|title=Hamilton Accies announce departure of seven first-team players|date=14 May 2018|accessdate=15 May 2018|author=Craig Fowler|work=The Scotsman}}</ref>

=== Arbroath ===
Jamieson then signed with [[Scottish League One|League One]] club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] in May 2018,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/2018/05/new-signing-darren-jamieson/ |title=Darren Jamieson |publisher=Arbroath FC |date=22 May 2018 |accessdate=22 May 2018 |archive-date=7 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180707010525/http://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/2018/05/new-signing-darren-jamieson/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> going on to win promotion to the [[Scottish Championship|Championship]] with the club as 2018–19 League One champions.<ref name=arbroath>{{cite web|title=ARBROATH'S TITLE IN NUMBERS|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/arbroaths-title-triumph-in-numbers|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=18 April 2019|accessdate=24 August 2019}}</ref>

=== Kelty Hearts ===
Jamieson signed for Lowland League side [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] in July 2020. Kelty gained promotion to [[Scottish League Two]] after winning the [[2020–21 Lowland Football League|2020-21 Lowland League]] which was curtailed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The following season, Jamieson featured in 35 of Kelty's 36 league matches as they won the [[2021–22 Scottish League Two]].<ref name=":0" /> Jamieson was again a key member of the squad for the 2022/23 campaign before departing at the end of the season upon expiry of his contract.

=== Airdrieonians (Loan) ===
On 13 May 2023, Jamieson joined [[Airdrieonians F.C.]] on an emergency loan deal and on the same day played the full match in a 1–0 victory against Falkirk in the [[2022–23 Scottish Championship]] play-off semi-final 2nd leg. Jamieson was an unused substitute for Airdie's match against former club Hamilton in the 1st leg of the final.

=== Stenhousemuir ===
On 18 May 2023, [[Stenhousemuir F.C.]] announced that Jamieson would join the club following his contract expiry at Kelty Hearts. On 24 January 2024, Jamieson's contract was extended to keep him at the club until the summer of 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stenhousemuir FC on X |url=https://twitter.com/StenhousemuirFC/status/1750135067307893042}}</ref> In his first season with The Warriors, Jamieson again won the [[Scottish League Two]] title for the [[2023–24 Scottish League Two|2023–24]] season keeping 19 clean sheets in 34 games. He was included in the [[PFA Scotland]] League Two team of the year.

|url=http://www.hamiltonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local-news/hamilton-news/2012/05/03/youngster-makes-first-team-debut-a-year-after-suffering-career-threatening-injury-51525-30888713/ |title=Youngster makes first-team debut a year after suffering career-threatening injury |publisher=Hamilton Advertiser |author=Andrew McGilvray |date=3 May 2012 |accessdate=2 July 2012}}</ref> In April 2013, Watson signed a two-year extension to his contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?view=article&catid=44:news&id=2220:watson-extends-contract&format=pdf|title=Watson extends contract|date=26 April 2013|publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C.|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130722230754/http://acciesfc.co.uk/index.php?view=article&catid=44%3Anews&id=2220%3Awatson-extends-contract&format=pdf|archivedate=22 July 2013}}</ref> In April 2015 he signed a new contract with the club, until the summer of 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32316758|title=Hamilton Academical: Six players sign new deals at Hamilton|date=15 April 2015|access-date=15 April 2015|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In September 2015, Watson moved on loan to [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] until January 2016. This loan spell was later extended until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/linn-commits-future-to-arbroath|title=Linn commits future to Arbroath | SPFL|website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref>

Watson left Hamilton at the end of the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/popular-duo-depart/|title=Popular duo depart|date=7 June 2017|accessdate=8 June 2017|publisher=Hamilton Academical F.C.}}</ref> He then signed for [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.eastfifefc.info/latest-news/235-latest-new-signings |title=Latest new signings |publisher=East Fife FC |date=12 July 2017 |accessdate=12 July 2017}}</ref> Watson made his debut for the club in the [[Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] against [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] on 15 July 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40619936 |title=Peterhead v East Fife |publisher=BBC |date=15 July 2017 |accessdate=16 July 2017}}</ref> He signed a new contract with the club in June 2018 <ref>{{cite web|url=https://eastfifefc.info/latest-news/490-jonathan-court-and-craig-watson-sign-on|title=Jonathan Court and Craig Watson Sign On|date=19 June 2018|accessdate=8 May 2019|publisher=East Fife F.C.}}</ref> and departed in May 2021 for [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.airdriefc.com/2021news/210529/Craig-Watson-agrees-terms|title=Craig Watson agrees terms|website=airdrie}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/ex-accies-star-snapped-up-24212071|title=Ex-Accies star snapped up by Airdrie|first=Andy|last=McGilvray|date=29 May 2021|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

'''Dale Carrick''' (born 7 January 1994)  is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]] for [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]]. Carrick started his career with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] and has also played for [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]], [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] and [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]]. Carrick has represented Scotland at both [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels.

==Career==
Born in Edinburgh, Carrick grew up supporting Hearts. A member of [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] Under-20 team <ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/page/Squad/DevelopmentTeamDetail/0,,10289,00.html |title=U20 team |publisher=[[Heart of Midlothian F.C.]] |work=heartsfc.co.uk |accessdate=4 August 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110901234010/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/page/Squad/DevelopmentTeamDetail/0%2C%2C10289%2C00.html |archivedate=1 September 2011 }}</ref> Carrick made his [[Scottish Premier League]] debut on 4 August 2012 in a 2–0 win versus [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19025830 | title=Hearts 2 – 0 St Johnstone | publisher=[[BBC]] | work=BBC Sport | date=4 August 2012 | access-date=4 August 2012}}</ref> On 23 August 2012 in only his second appearance, Carrick made his [[UEFA|European]] debut as a substitute in a 1–0 defeat versus [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at [[Tynecastle Stadium|Tynecastle]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19279553 | title=Hearts 0–1 Liverpool | publisher=[[BBC]] | work=BBC Sport | date=23 August 2012 | access-date=23 August 2012}}</ref> Carrick's first goal for the ''Jambos'' arrived on 18 January 2014 in a thrilling 3–3 draw versus the [[Perth, Scotland|Perth]] club at [[McDiarmid Park]].<ref>{{cite web|title=St Johnstone 3-3 Hearts|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25693251|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Lindsay|first=Clive|date=18 January 2014}}</ref>

Carrick had joined [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on 30 January 2015 on a one-month loan deal.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.raithrovers.net/18022/rovers-secure-hearts-star-on-loan-deal.htm | title=Rovers Secure Hearts Star on Loan Deal | publisher=[[Raith Rovers F.C.]] | work=raithrovers.net | date=30 January 2015 | accessdate=30 January 2015}}</ref> The loan deal was then cut-short on 11 February 2015 as a result of Carrick suffering an injury.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/championship/on-loan-raith-striker-returns-to-hearts-following-injury-1.835176 | title=On-loan Raith striker returns to Hearts following injury | publisher=[[The Courier (Dundee)]] | work=thecourier.co.uk | date=11 February 2015 | accessdate=11 February 2015}}</ref>

On 8 July 2015, Carrick departed the [[Tynecastle Stadium|Tynecastle]] club to pursue regular first-team football elsewhere with his contract terminated by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|title=CARRICK EXITS HEARTS|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/4434|publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=8 July 2015|accessdate=8 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thenational.scot/sport/football-carrick-allowed-to-leave-hearts.4979|title = Football: Carrick allowed to leave Hearts| date=9 July 2015 }}</ref> Carrick then signed a three-year contract with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/1324351-dale-carrick-signs-three-year-deal-with-kilmarnock-after-leaving-hearts/ |title=Dale Carrick signs three year deal with Kilmarnock after leaving Hearts |first=Jamie |last=Borthwick |work=STV Sport |publisher=STV |date=9 July 2015 |accessdate=9 July 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304092414/http://sport.stv.tv/football/1324351-dale-carrick-signs-three-year-deal-with-kilmarnock-after-leaving-hearts/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

After one season with ''Killie'' Carrick then signed for the [[West Lothian]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in July 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://livingstonfc.co.uk/dale-carrick-signs/?platform=hootsuite |title=Dale Carrick signs on |publisher=Livingston FC |date=15 July 2016 |accessdate=15 July 2016}}</ref> On 26 January 2017 Carrick moved on loan to [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]] for the remainder of the [[2016–17 in Scottish football|2016-17]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://livingstonfc.co.uk/carrick-blue-brazil-switch/ |title=Carrick in Blue Brazil switch |publisher=Livingston FC |date=26 January 2017 |accessdate=26 January 2017}}</ref> Carrick departed the ''Lions'' in January 2018 and signed for [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] in an attempt to get more first-team football.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://livingstonfc.co.uk/dale-moves-diamonds/ |title=Dale moves to the Diamonds |publisher=Livingston FC |date=11 January 2018 |accessdate=11 January 2018}}</ref> He remained at Airdrie until May 2021.

On 28 May 2021, Carrick signed for [[Scottish League Two]] side [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=28 May 2021|title=New signing: Dale Carrick|url=https://www.stirlingalbionfc.co.uk/new-signing-dale-carrick/|url-status=live|access-date=28 May 2021|website=stirlingalbionfc.co.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210528181920/https://www.stirlingalbionfc.co.uk/new-signing-dale-carrick/ |archive-date=28 May 2021 }}</ref>

On 2 August 2025, Carrick signed for [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web | title=New Signing: Dale Carrick Signs for 25/26 Season | date=2 August 2025 | url=https://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/2025/08/02/dale-carrick-signs-for-25-26-season/ }}</ref>

===Scotland===
Carrick has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] level. Carrick made his debut in an International Challenge match versus [[Jersey]] on 18 August 2009<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/international_fixture_details.cfm?page=1921&matchID=90484 | title=Jersey v Scotland International Challenge Match | publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] | work=scottishfa.co.uk | date=18 August 2009 | accessdate=5 August 2012}}</ref> and made four appearances in total.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=2492&playerID=64647&squadID=17 | title=Dale Carrick | publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] | work=scottishfa.co.uk | accessdate=5 August 2012}}</ref>
