'''Thomas 'Tam''''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cairns |first=Craig |date=2023-12-12 |title=Arbroath's Tam O'Brien gives first impressions of new boss ahead of taking on 'flying' Raith Rovers |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/4838125/arbroaths-tam-obrien-on-new-boss-jim-mcintyre/ |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref> '''O'Brien''' (born 7 August 1991) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|central defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} side [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]], where he is also club captain<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-24 |title=Thomas O’Brien Contract Extension |url=https://arbroathfc.co.uk/thomas-obrien-contract-extension/#:~:text=31-year-old%20Thomas%20signed,as%20becoming%20our%20Club%20Captain. |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=Arbroath FC |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
O'Brien began his footballing career at [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]'s Academy, but moved to [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]] in 2003. He signed professional terms in 2007, and after loan spells with [[Rosyth F.C.|Rosyth]] and [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]],<ref>[http://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/juniors/articles/2010/03/04/397733-size-matters-insists-kelty-hearts-boss/ Size matters insists Kelty Hearts boss]; Dunfermline Press, 4 March 2010</ref> he made his first team debut on 7 August 2010, in a 2–0 home loss against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_div_1/8890473.stm Cowdenbeath 0–2 Ross County]; [[BBC Sport]], 7 August 2010</ref> O'Brien scored his first professional goal on 1 October 2011, in a 1–1 away draw against [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>[http://spfl.co.uk/league-one/fixture/3407733/ Arbroath 1–1 Cowdenbeath]; [[Scottish Professional Football League|SPFL]], 1 October 2011</ref>

At the end of the [[2014–15 in Scottish football|2014–15 season]], O'Brien signed a two-year contract with [[Scottish League One]] side [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Tom O'Brien joins the 'Loons' |url=https://www.forfarathletic.co.uk/item/1833-tom-obrien-joins-the-loons|publisher=Forfar Athletic F.C.|date=28 May 2015|accessdate=25 August 2019}}</ref> He spent two seasons with Forfar, and was named in the [[2016–17 in Scottish football|2016–17]] [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#League Two 4|PFA Scotland League Two Team of the Year]] after helping his club return to League One.<ref name=team>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39819482 |title=Liam Lindsay with Celtic & Dons players in Premiership team of the year |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=5 May 2017 |accessdate=1 June 2017}}</ref>

O'Brien subsequently signed a two-year deal with [[Angus, Scotland|Angus]] rivals Arbroath on 1 June 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thomas O'Brien and Danny Denholm|url=http://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/2017/06/thomas-obrien-and-danny-denholm/|publisher=Arbroath F.C.|date=1 June 2017|accessdate=1 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180409043916/http://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/2017/06/thomas-obrien-and-danny-denholm/|archive-date=9 April 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In [[2018–19 in Scottish football|2019]], O'Brien was part of the Arbroath squad that won the [[Scottish League One]] title, gaining promotion to the [[Scottish Championship]]. The ''Lichties'' would remain in the second tier for five seasons, the last three of which were spent as the only part-time club in the division, with O'Brien ever-present throughout much of this time. This included a memorable promotion challenge in season [[2021–22 Scottish Championship|2021-22]], with Arbroath eventually succumbing to champions [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on the penultimate matchday.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-03-01 |title=Dick Campbell on 'miracle' Arbroath season and 'irritating' exit |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68444218 |access-date=2025-04-14 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Persistent injuries in the [[2023–24 Scottish Championship|2023–24]] season limited O'Brien to just 19 league appearances, as Arbroath were relegated from the Championship.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-04-13 |title=Ayr United 5-0 Arbroath: Visitors relegated as Ayr move to sixth |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68747637 |access-date=2025-04-14 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In April 2025, O'Brien captained Arbroath to the [[Scottish League One]] title with three games to spare, following a 4-0 victory over [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] that secured an immediate return to the Championship.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-13 |title=The inside story of how Arbroath went from being League 1 bottom dogs to champions |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/25086030.arbroath-went-league-1-bottom-dogs-champions/ |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=The Herald |language=en}}</ref>

'''Gregor Buchanan''' (born 31 March 1990) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Stenhous}} club [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] where he is the club's captain.

After progressing through [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]]'s youth academy, Buchanan played for [[Scottish Junior Football Association|Scottish Junior]] clubs [[Armadale Thistle F.C.|Armadale Thistle]] and [[Bathgate Thistle F.C.|Bathgate Thistle]]. Buchanan later played for [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] (first spell), [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]], [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] and [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]].

==Early and personal life==
Buchanan is originally from [[Falkirk]] in [[Stirlingshire]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/defender-from-falkirk-who-helped-st-mirren-and-livingston-out-of-the-championship-and-into-the-spfl-premiership-1-4749001|title=Defender from Falkirk who helped St Mirren and Livingston out of the Championship and into the SPFL Premiership|website=www.falkirkherald.co.uk|last=Oliver|first=David|date=3 June 2018}}</ref>

==Career==
Buchanan was released by [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] at the age of sixteen.<ref name = "promotion"/> Buchanan then played with [[Scottish Junior Football Association|Scottish Junior]] clubs [[Armadale Thistle F.C.|Armadale Thistle]] and [[Bathgate Thistle F.C.|Bathgate Thistle]],<ref name = "Signs for Dunfermline"/> before signing for [[Scottish Football League First Division|Scottish First Division]] club [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrie United]] in July 2012.<ref name = "airdrie"/> In his first season with ''The Diamonds'', Buchanan was part of the team that finished bottom of [[2012–13 Scottish First Division|the final]] Scottish First Division. In the [[2013–14 Scottish League One|2013–14 season]], Buchanan helped the club to a mid-table finish and after some impressive performances was signed by fellow [[Scottish League One]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].<ref name = "Signs for Dunfermline"/>

A few weeks after leaving the Pars, Buchanan signed for [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] and was [[Stephen Aitken]]'s first signing for the club in May 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=1883 |title=Stevie makes first signing |access-date=28 May 2015|publisher=dumbartonfootballclub.com|last=Findlay|first=Alan|date=28 May 2015}}</ref> Buchanan renewed his contract at the end of the [[2015–16 in Scottish football|2015-16]] season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Defender Buchanan returns |url=https://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=2489|publisher=Dumbarton F.C.|last=Findlay|first=Alan|date=3 June 2016|access-date=3 June 2016}}</ref>

Buchanan departed the Sons after 77 appearances, scoring three goals and then signed for [[Scottish Championship]] rivals [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on a one-year deal in May 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/911-buchanan-and-stewart-are-buddies |title=Buchanan and Stewart are Buddies |publisher=St Mirren FC |date=26 May 2017 |access-date=26 May 2017}}</ref> Prior to turning professional with St Mirren, as a part-time player, Buchanan worked as an insurance salesman.<ref name = "promotion"/> After limited chances to play for the Buddies, Buchanan departed the club by mutual consent on 11 January 2018 and signed for [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/buchanan-signs-saints/?platform=hootsuite |title=Buchanan signs from Saints |publisher=Livingston.co.uk |date=11 January 2018 |access-date=11 January 2018}}</ref> Both of the clubs Buchanan represented in the [[2017–18 in Scottish football|2017-18]] season, the ''Buddies'' and the ''Lions'', were promoted from the [[Scottish Championship]].<ref name = "promotion"/> Buchanan was awarded a Championship winner's medal for his time at the Buddies.<ref name = "promotion">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44304744 |title=Gregor Buchanan's 'fairytale story' of double promotion after sister's illness |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |first=Clive |last=Lindsay |date=1 June 2018 |access-date=8 June 2018}}</ref>

Buchanan signed a one-year deal with [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] in June 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gmfc.net/2018/06/08/gregor-buchanan-signs-for-morton/ |title=Gregor Buchanan signs for Morton |publisher=Greenock Morton F.C. |date=8 June 2018 |access-date=8 June 2018}}</ref> In June 2019, Buchanan signed for home-town club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/falkirk-bring-gregor-buchanan-home-from-morton-as-ray-mckinnon-seals-second-signing-of-the-day-1-4944624|title=Falkirk bring Gregor Buchanan home from Morton as Ray McKinnon seals second signing of the day|website=www.falkirkherald.co.uk|last=Oliver|first=David|date=10 June 2019}}</ref> Buchanan departed the Bairns at the end of the [[2019–20 in Scottish football|2019-20]] season, after being appointed club captain that season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/pictures-nine-players-departing-falkirk-summer-2884516|title=IN PICTURES: The nine players departing Falkirk this summer|website=www.falkirkherald.co.uk |date=15 June 2020 }}</ref>

On 24 August 2020, Buchanan signed for [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] until 31 May 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.falkirkherald.co.uk/sport/football/falkirk-fc/former-falkirk-duo-make-championship-moves-another-poised-hearts-2945318|title=Former Falkirk duo make Championship moves, with another poised for Hearts|website=www.falkirkherald.co.uk |date=18 August 2020 }}</ref>

On 12 February 2021, Buchanan captained Queens in his 300th club career match versus [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] as the match ended in a 1-1 draw at [[Palmerston Park]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.qosfc.com/match-2226|title=QoS : Report - Heart of Midlothian 12.2.21|website=www.qosfc.com}}</ref>

On 12 June 2021, after leaving the ''Doonhamers'', Buchanan returned to [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]], signing a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dumbarton Football Club - BUCHANAN IS BACK!|url=https://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=4962|access-date=12 June 2021|website=www.dumbartonfootballclub.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=4964|title=Dumbarton Football Club - EXCLUSIVE: BUCHANAN AIMS HIGH ON HIS RETURN|website=www.dumbartonfootballclub.com}}</ref> He was named the club's vice-captain in June 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dumbarton Football Club - MCGEEVER IS NEW CLUB CAPTAIN |url=https://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=5403 |access-date=27 June 2022 |website=www.dumbartonfootballclub.com}}</ref> He left the club in May 2023 after turning down the offer of a new deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crawford |first=Jack |date=2023-05-26 |title=GREGOR SET FOR NEW CHALLENGE |url=https://dumbartonfootballclub.com/33275-2/ |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=Dumbarton Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Colin Hamilton''' (born 7 May 1992) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defender (association football)|defender]] for and co-manages {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] with [[David Gold (footballer)|David Gold]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cql3lz1plv7o|title=Hamilton and Gold confirmed as new Arbroath player-managers|date=12 September 2024|website=BBC}}</ref>

He began his career at [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] and moved to [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] in 2009. He never played for Hearts, and made his debut on loan back at Stenhousemuir in the [[Scottish Football League Second Division]], where he later represented [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] and [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]]. He spent the 2015–16 season at [[Alloa Athletic]] before returning to Arbroath.

==Career==

===Heart of Midlothian===
A former youth player at [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]], Hamilton was signed by [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] in March 2009.<ref name=sten>{{cite news|last1=Bulloch|first1=Terry|title=Warriors Transfer Brothers|url=http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2009/03/12/28/|accessdate=23 August 2015|publisher=[[Stenhousemuir F.C.]]|date=12 March 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161017153323/http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2009/03/12/28/|archive-date=17 October 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was first included in a matchday squad on 15 May 2011, remaining an unused substitute as they concluded the [[Scottish Premier League]] season with a 2–1 defeat at [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Dundee Utd 2 – 1 Hearts|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/9484607.stm|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 May 2011}}</ref>

In September 2011, Hamilton returned to Stenhousemuir on loan.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hamilton returns home|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/hamilton-returns-home/|accessdate=23 August 2015|publisher=[[Scottish Professional Football League]]|date=30 September 2011}}</ref> He made his debut on 24 September, playing the full 90 minutes as they defeated [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] 2–1 at [[Ochilview Park]] in the [[Scottish Football League Second Division|Second Division]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Stenhousemuir 2–1 East Fife|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15027713|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=24 September 2011}}</ref> A week later he scored his first goal, a header in a 5–2 loss at [[Airdrie United]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Airdrie Utd 5–2 Stenhousemuir|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15137013|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 October 2011}}</ref> On 19 October, his loan was extended until 24 December, the maximum 91 days.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Bulloch|first1=Terry|title=Colin Hamilton Loan Period Extended|url=http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2011/10/19/625/|accessdate=23 August 2015|publisher=Stenhousemuir F.C.|date=19 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924110240/http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/news/2011/10/19/625/|archive-date=24 September 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Arbroath===
In 2012, Hamilton joined another Second Division team, [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]], and made his debut on 18 August in a 4–2 win over [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] at [[Gayfield Park]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Arbroath 4–2 Ayr United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19292089|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 August 2012}}</ref> His first goal for the club came on 9 February 2013, the only goal of an away victory at [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Albion Rovers 0–1 Arbroath|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21394393|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 February 2013}}</ref> He made 32 league appearances in his first season at Arbroath, scoring once more, an equaliser in a 4–2 win at [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] on 30 March.<ref>{{cite news|title=Smokies too hot to handle|url=http://spfl.co.uk/league-one/fixture/3520038/|accessdate=23 August 2015|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=30 March 2013}}</ref>

In July 2013, he trialled at English club [[Notts County]], but the transfer collapsed.<ref>{{cite news|title=Arbroath hope to get Hamilton back|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/arbroath-hope-to-get-hamilton-back/|accessdate=23 August 2015|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=19 July 2013}}</ref> On 24 August, Hamilton was sent off after half an hour for conceding a penalty in an eventual 2–1 defeat at [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]].<ref>{{cite news|title=East Fife 2–1 Arbroath: Two see red as Fifers fly at Bayview|url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/east-fife/237231-east-fife-2-1-arbroath-two-see-red-as-fifers-fly-at-bayview/|accessdate=23 August 2015|publisher=STV Sport|date=24 August 2013}}</ref> He made 35 league appearances in his second campaign at Arbroath, scoring in a 4–3 home defeat to former club Stenhousemuir on 21 September.<ref>{{cite news|title=Arbroath 3–4 Stenhousemuir|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24170022|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=21 September 2013}}</ref>

===Brechin City===
On 22 May 2014, Hamilton joined fellow [[Scottish League One]] club [[Brechin City]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Colin Hamilton Joins The City|url=http://www.brechincity.com/bcfc/servlet/BCFCFrontControllerServlet?action=News&page_id=1471&category=2|accessdate=23 August 2015|publisher=[[Brechin City F.C.]]|date=22 May 2014}}</ref> He made his debut on 26 July in the first round of the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]], playing the full 90 minutes in a 3–1 win at [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Cowdenbeath 1–3 Brechin|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28382108|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 July 2014}}</ref> On 23 August, he scored his first goal for the club, heading the opening goal of a 2–2 draw away to [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Stranraer 2–2 Brechin|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28816783|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=23 August 2014}}</ref> He was sent off on 11 November for two bookings in a 2–1 win over [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]] at [[Glebe Park, Brechin|Glebe Park]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Brechin 2–1 Stirling|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29860343|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 November 2014}}</ref>

On 29 November, Hamilton headed the opening goal away to [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]] in the [[Scottish Cup]] fourth round, but it ended in a 1–1 draw;<ref>{{cite news|title=Annan Athletic 1–1 Brechin|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30156824|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 November 2014}}</ref> ten days later he scored again in the replay, a 4–2 victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=Brechin 4–2 Annan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30287779|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 December 2014}}</ref> He was sent off for a second time on 14 March 2015 in a 3–0 loss at [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Peterhead 3–0 Brechin|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31776716|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 March 2015}}</ref> Hamilton played 32 League One games in his only season at Brechin, and also took part with them in the play-offs for promotion to the [[Scottish Championship]], where they lost 2–1 on aggregate to [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] in the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite news|title=Alloa 0–1 Brechin|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32570387|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 May 2015|archive-date=6 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150706210027/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/32570387|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Alloa Athletic===
On 21 May 2015, Hamilton became Alloa's first signing after securing their Championship status.<ref>{{cite news|title=Alloa bring in Hamilton|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/alloa-bring-in-hamilton/|accessdate=23 August 2015|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=21 May 2015}}</ref> He made his debut on 25 July, playing the full 90 minutes as they won 1–0 at [[Highland Football League|Highland League]] team [[Brora Rangers]] in the first round of the Challenge Cup.<ref>{{cite news|title=Brora Rangers 0–1 Alloa|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33578672|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 July 2015}}</ref> On 8 August he played his first game in a professional league, a 3–1 loss away to [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Queen of Sth 3–1 Alloa|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33744879|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=8 August 2015}}</ref>

He scored his first Alloa goal on 19 September, a last-minute equaliser against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] at the [[Indodrill Stadium]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Alloa Athletic 1–1 Rangers|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34230449|accessdate=13 April 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|date=19 September 2015}}</ref> and added a second on 9 February 2016 to start a comeback to earn a 2–2 home draw against [[Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Alloa Athletic 2–2 Greenock Morton|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35525772|accessdate=13 April 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 February 2016}}</ref> However, Alloa were relegated at the end of the season.

===Return to Arbroath===
Prior to the 2016–17 season, Hamilton returned to Arbroath, now in League Two.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arbroath add Thomson to squad |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/arbroath-add-thomson-to-squad |accessdate=31 January 2019 |publisher=Scottish Professional Football League |date=6 July 2016}}</ref> In his first match back for the Red Lichties, he scored a last-minute equaliser to earn a 1–1 draw at home to Championship club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in the group stages of the League Cup.<ref>{{cite news |title=League Cup: Dundee United beat Arbroath on penalties, Raith defeat Cove Rangers |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36809985 |accessdate=31 January 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=15 July 2016}}</ref> His team won promotion at the end of the season as champions.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arbroath are League Two champions! |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/arbroath-are-league-2-champions |accessdate=31 January 2019 |publisher=Scottish Professional Football League |date=6 May 2017}}</ref>

On 21 April 2018, Hamilton scored in a 2–0 home win over [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] to seal a spot in the play-offs for a potential second consecutive promotion.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arbroath 2 Airdrieonians 0: Red Lichties not in play-offs to make up numbers |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/scottish-league-1/640805/arbroath-2-airdrieonians-0-red-lichties-not-in-play-offs-to-make-up-numbers/ |accessdate=31 January 2019 |work=The Courier |date=23 April 2018}}</ref> However, they lost in the semi-finals to [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]].

==Personal life==
Hamilton's younger brother [[Jack Hamilton (goalkeeper)|Jack]] also became a footballer. A [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]], he went from Stenhousemuir's academy to Hearts at the same time.<ref name=sten/>

'''Kyle Magennis''' (born 26 August 1998) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.stmirren.com/kyle-magennis|title=Kyle Magennis|publisher=St Mirren FC|access-date=21 April 2017|archive-date=13 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180813075002/https://www.stmirren.com/kyle-magennis|url-status=dead}}</ref> He has previously played for [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], and also represented [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] at [[Scotland national under-20 football team|under-17]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] level.

==Club career==

=== St Mirren ===
Born in [[Glasgow]], Magennis attended [[Paisley Grammar School]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/coaching-masterclass-paisley-grammars-prize-2569559|title=Coaching masterclass for Paisley Grammar's prize guys|date=27 June 2011}}</ref> Magennis joined [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]'s youth academy at the age of five<ref name="bio"/> and remained there throughout his youth career until making his debut for the senior team against [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in October 2016, aged 18, in the [[Scottish Championship]].<ref name="bio" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37737901|title=Hibernian 2–0 St Mirren|website=BBC Sport |date=29 October 2016|first=Brian |last=McLauchlin |access-date=21 April 2017}}</ref> He continued to appear for the club throughout the season, scoring his first goal for the club in a narrow win over [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/q-of-south-vs-st-mirren/357282|title=Queen of the South 2–3 St Mirren|website=Sky Sports|date=6 December 2016|access-date=21 April 2017}}</ref> Having impressed manager [[Jack Ross (footballer, born 1976)|Jack Ross]] with his performances, he was offered a new contract with St Mirren in December 2016 which extended his contract with the club until summer 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/club-news/417-kyle-magennis-signs-new-contract|title=Kyle Magennis signs new contract|publisher=St Mirren FC|date=9 December 2016 |access-date=21 April 2017}}</ref>

Now established as a first team player in the ''Saints'' squad, Magennis signed a new contract committing him to the club until the summer of 2020,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/904-delight-as-kyle-magennis-signs-till-2020 |title=Delight as Kyle Magennis signs till 2020|publisher=St Mirren FC|date=24 May 2017|access-date=24 May 2017}}</ref> and after clinching the [[2017–18 Scottish Championship]] title, he further extended his contract with St Mirren to 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44589117 |title=St Mirren extend Kyle Magennis contract as Brian Rice becomes assistant to Stubbs |website=BBC Sport |date=23 June 2018 |accessdate=24 June 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/1943-delight-for-saints-as-kyle-magennis-agrees-contract-extension |title=Delight for Saints as Kyle Magennis agrees contract extension |publisher=St Mirren FC|date=23 June 2018|access-date=24 May 2017}}</ref> He was in the side which secured their status in the [[Scottish Premiership]] via the relegation playoff in May 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48324854|title=St Mirren 1–1 Dundee United|website=BBC Sport |date=26 May 2019|access-date=11 August 2019}}</ref>

Magennis and Saints suffered a major blow in January 2020, when he injured his knee during a 1–0 defeat to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], ending his season after having appeared in every match of the campaign until suffering the injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51216504 |title=Kyle Magennis: St Mirren midfielder will miss rest of season |website=BBC Sport |date=24 January 2020 |accessdate=26 January 2020}}</ref> In September 2020, St Mirren stated they had rejected a "substantial" offer for Magennis from Hibernian.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54333352 |title=St Mirren: Paisley club say Hibs' Magennis bid rejected |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=28 September 2020 |accessdate=28 September 2020}}</ref> A few days later another offer from the same club was accepted.<ref name = "BBC hibs">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54391305 |title=Kyle Magennis: Hibernian sign midfielder on five-year deal from St Mirren |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=5 October 2020 |accessdate=5 October 2020}}</ref>

=== Hibernian ===
Magennis signed a five-year deal with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 5 October 2020.<ref name = "BBC hibs"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/10763 |title=Kyle Magennis Is A Hibee |website=www.hibernianfc.co.uk |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=5 October 2020 |accessdate=5 October 2020 |archive-date=9 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201009113746/http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/10763 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 1 August 2021, Magennis scored [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]'s opening [[Scottish Premiership]] goal for the [[2021–22 Hibernian F.C. season|2021–22]] season against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] which ended in a 3–2 victory for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57958660|title=Motherwell 2–3 Hibernian|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Martin|last=Watt|date=1 August 2021|access-date=1 August 2021}}</ref> Magennis had a good start to the 2021–22 season, but then missed most of it due to groin and knee injuries.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60988849 |title=Hibs: Kyle Magennis ruled out after surgery |website=BBC Sport |date=4 April 2022 |accessdate=5 April 2022}}</ref>

After he suffered from more injury problems during the 2022–23 season, Magennis was allowed to leave Hibs in June 2023.<ref name = killie/>

===Kilmarnock===
Following his release by Hibs, Magennis signed a two-year contract with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on 21 June 2023.<ref name = killie>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/ckk9xy73evqo | title=Hibs annul Magennis contract to allow him to join Killie |website=BBC Sport | date=21 June 2023 | accessdate=21 June 2023}}</ref>

Magennis signed a new one-year contract with Kilmarnock in July 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/clym3qd6z5go |title=Midfielder Kyle Magennis signs one-year contract with Kilmarnock |website=BBC Sport | date=2 July 2025 | accessdate=2 July 2025}}</ref>

===Arbroath===
On 11 September 2026, Magennis signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Magennis is a Lichtie |url=https://x.com/ArbroathFC/status/2098434019079622932 |access-date=17 October 2026 |work=Arbroath FC |date=11 September 2026}}</ref>

== International career ==
Magennis was selected for the [[Scotland national under-20 football team|Scotland under-20]] squad in the [[2017 Toulon Tournament]],<ref>{{ cite web | title = Scotland squad for Toulon announced | url = http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1957&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=16955 | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 17 May 2017 | access-date = 1 July 2022 }}</ref> in which they won the bronze medal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-finish-third-at-toulon-tournament-with-3-0-win/ | title = Scotland finish third at Toulon Tournament with 3-0 win | publisher = [[Scottish Football Association]] | date = 10 June 2017 | access-date = 1 July 2022}}</ref> It was the nation's first ever medal at the competition.<ref name = "bronze"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the-gazette.co.uk/sport/15391284.paisley-2021-stadium-to-host-european-under-21-championship-qualifier/|title = Paisley 2021 stadium to host European Under-21 Championship qualifier| date=5 July 2017 }}</ref> He then played for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] team, making his debut in a 2–1 win against the [[Netherlands national under-21 football team|Netherlands]] in September 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-seal-dutch-double-in-dramatic-style/?rid=13925 |title=Scotland seal Dutch double in dramatic style |publisher=Scottish Football Association |date=11 September 2018 |accessdate=12 September 2018}}</ref>

'''Nikolay Todorov''' ({{langx|bg|Николай Тодоров}}; born 24 August 1996) is a Bulgarian [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a forward for Queen's Park football club .

Todorov was a [[Bulgaria national under-21 football team|Bulgaria U21]] international. Known for his physical presence, At the age of 7, Todorov started his career with [[OFC Spartak Pleven|Spartak Pleven]]'s [[youth system]] before winning a scholarship in England. In 2014, he joined [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] in their Under-21s academy, loan spells followed at [[Hemel Hempstead F.C.|Hemel Hempstead]] and [[Worcester City F.C.|Worcester City]] in England.

Todorov joined [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] in 2016, loan spells followed at [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]] and [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] where he was part of the [[2017–18 in Scottish football|2017–18]] promotion winning team finishing as champions. He spent the first half of the [[2017–18 in Scottish football|2017–18]] season back on loan at Livingston, before spending the second half of the season at [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]]. He subsequently had a short spell in Italy with [[F.C. Rieti|Rieti]], before returning to Scotland with [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] and then [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]]. Todorov signed for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline]] in June 2021, winning the [[Scottish League One|League One]] title in 2023.<ref name="auto">{{cite web | url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/dunfermline-athletic-win-cinch-league-1 | title=Dunfermline Athletic win cinch League 1 | SPFL }}</ref> Todorov left Dunfermline at the end of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Squad_Update&ID=14378 | title=Squad Update | date=2023-05-07 | website=dafc.co.uk}}</ref> He then joined [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] for a season, with whom he won the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]].

==Career==
Born in [[Pleven]], Todorov joined FC Pleven's Academy at seven years old.<ref name=ОтПлевен>{{cite web |first=Ralitsa |last=Yotova |title=От Плевен до шампиона на Европа - историята на Николай Тодоров |publisher=topsport.bg |url=https://topsport.bg/bulgarians-abroad/ot-pleven-do-shampiona-na-evropa-istoriyata-na-nikolay-todorov.html |date=18 April 2016 |access-date=25 April 2017 |language=bg}}</ref> In 2011, he joined Brooke House College and played three years for the college's football team, Brooke House College Football Academy under manager Ben Watts.

In 2014, Todorov joined [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] at Under-21 level.<ref>{{cite web |title=From Pleven to the champion of Europe |url=http://premierleaguepredictions.online/from-pleven-to-the-champion-of-europe-the-story-of-nikolai-todorov/ |website=premierleaguepredictions.online |date=29 August 2016 |access-date=25 April 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519112242/http://premierleaguepredictions.online/from-pleven-to-the-champion-of-europe-the-story-of-nikolai-todorov/ |archive-date=19 May 2017 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> On 10 January 2015, he signed his second professional contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web |title=Four Nottingham Forest youngsters have signed professional contracts with the club |url=http://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/article/academy-pro-contracts-100215-2260646.aspx |publisher=Nottingham Forest F.C. |date=10 February 2015}}</ref> Although he played for the Under-21s, he failed to feature for the first team and was officially released in May 2016.<ref>{{cite web |title=Retained list 2016 |url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2016/may/retained-list-2016/ |publisher=Nottingham Forest F.C. |date=27 May 2016 |access-date=5 July 2018}}</ref>

Todorov had already joined up with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] in April 2016, to try earn himself a contract.<ref>{{cite news |first=Barry |last=Anderson |title=Hearts take Bulgarian striker on trial |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-take-bulgarian-striker-on-trial-1-4096587 |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=11 April 2016 |access-date=5 July 2018}}</ref> After a successful two-month trial period, he then signed a one-year contract in June 2016.<ref>{{cite web |title=Talented youngsters join club |url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/5204 |publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C. |date=15 June 2016 |access-date=5 July 2018 |archive-date=5 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180705001842/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/5204 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In July 2016, Todorov had a six-month loan spell at [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Alasdair |last=Mackenzie |title=Hearts youngster Nikolay Todorov joins Cowdenbeath on six-month loan |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/14645359.Hearts_youngster_Nikolay_Todorov_joins_Cowdenbeath_on_six-month_loan/ |newspaper=The Herald (Glasgow) |date=27 July 2016 |access-date=5 July 2018}}</ref> He made his debut on the opening day of the [[2016–17 in Scottish football|2016–17]] season in a 1–0 home defeat to [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]] on 6 August 2016.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cowdenbeath 0–1 Elgin |url=http://www.cowdenbeathfc.com/index.php?act=viewReport&docId=503 |publisher=Cowdenbeath F.C. |date=6 August 2016 |access-date=5 July 2018}}</ref> The following week, Todorov scored his first ever league goal in a 4–3 away loss at [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]], with a header from a cross six yards out in the 59th minute.<ref>{{cite news |title=Forfar 4–3 Cowdenbeath |url=http://www.cowdenbeathfc.com/index.php?act=viewReport&docId=504 |publisher=Cowdenbeath F.C. |date=13 August 2016 |access-date=5 July 2018}}</ref> Todorov was mainly played as a [[centre back]] due to an injury crisis, before being recalled by Hearts in January 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bulgarian recalled by Hearts |url=http://www.centralfifetimes.com/news/15033874.Cowden_will_have_to_battle_on_without_Todorov/ |newspaper=Central Fife Times & Advertiser |date=19 January 2017 |access-date=5 July 2018}}</ref> Todorov then went on loan to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in January 2017,<ref name=AcoHfNT>{{cite web |title=Change of Heart for Nikolay Todorov |url=http://livingstonfc.co.uk/change-heart-nikolay-todorov/ |publisher=Livingston F.C. |date=23 January 2017 |access-date=5 July 2018}}</ref> helping Livingston win the [[2016–17 Scottish League One]] title.<ref name=SLOPromotion>{{cite web |title=Livingston 2–1 Alloa Athletic |url=http://livingstonfc.co.uk/livingston-2-1-alloa-athletic/ |publisher=Livingston F.C. |date=8 April 2017 |access-date=8 April 2017}}</ref> He signed a new one-year contract with Hearts at the end of the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=New deal for Todorov |url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/5930 |publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C. |date=12 May 2017 |access-date=5 July 2018}}</ref> Todorov spent the first half of the [[2017–18 in Scottish football|2017–18]] season back on loan at Livingston.<ref>{{cite web |title=Todorov returns to Livingston on loan |url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/todorov-returns-to-livingston-on-loan/ |publisher=SPFL |date=24 June 2017 |access-date=26 June 2017}}</ref>

On 31 January 2018, Todorov joined [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2017–18 in Scottish football|2017–18]] season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Todorov Signs |url=http://www.qosfc.com/news-3908 |publisher=Queen of the South F.C. |access-date=31 January 2018}}</ref>

On 14 August 2018, Todorov signed a two-year contract with Italian [[Serie C]] club [[F.C. Rieti|Rieti]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Corriere di Rieti|url=https://corrieredirieti.corr.it/news/sport/503895/un-ariete-bulgaro-per-il-rieti-ingaggiato-nikolay-todorov.html|title=Un "ariete" bulgaro per il Rieti: ingaggiato Nikolay Todorov|date=14 August 2018|language=it}}</ref> He then returned to Scottish football in January 2019, signing for [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46994524|title = Scottish Championship January ins and outs|work = BBC Sport}}</ref> Following Falkirk's relegation to [[Scottish League One|League One]], he left and signed for [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].

Todorov spent two seasons with [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline]] before signing for [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] in June 2023, where he scored the winner in a 3–2 win against his former club, Inverness.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/news/23587509.dunfermline-nikolay-todorov-discusses-exit-making-airdrie-move/|title = Nikolay Todorov discusses exit before making Airdrie move|work = Dunfermline Press|date=13 June 2023}}</ref> Todorov enjoyed a successful season with the ''Diamonds'', scoring the winning penalty in the [[2024 Scottish Challenge Cup final]] and helped the club reach the [[2023–24 Scottish Premiership#Premiership play-offs|Premiership play-offs]] as the club's top scorer.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=2024-03-24 |title=SPFL Trust Cup final: Reaction as Airdrieonians beat The New Saints |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/68592538 |access-date=2024-07-20 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-06 |title=Scottish Premiership: Airdrieonians & Partick eye top tier |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cw4d2gvpyxdo |access-date=2024-07-20 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In July 2024, Todorov joined Airdrie's [[Lanarkshire derby#Hamilton vs Airdrie|Lanarkshire rivals]] and fellow [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-19 |title=NIKOLAY TODOROV JOINS ACCIES - Hamilton Accies |url=https://hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/nikolay-todorov-joins-accies/ |access-date=2024-07-20 |website=hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Todorov has represented Bulgaria on U15, U16 and U21 level. On 30 May 2017, he received his first call-up for [[Bulgaria national under-21 football team|Bulgaria U21]] for the friendly matches against [[Georgia national under-21 football team|Georgia U21]] and [[Greece national under-21 football team|Greece U21]] on 8 and 12 June 2017.<ref name="geogre">{{cite web |title=Съставът на България U21 за контролите с Грузия и Гърция |url=http://www.bfunion.bg/news/7922 |publisher=Bulgarian Football Union |date=30 May 2017 |access-date=31 May 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170823165152/http://www.bfunion.bg/news/7922 |archive-date=23 August 2017 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

==Style of play==
Todorov primarily plays as a [[centre forward]], but he can also be deployed as a [[centre back]]. A two‑footed player, he is capable of scoring with either foot and is noted for his strength, physical presence, and aerial ability.<ref name=AcoHfNT/>

==Personal life==
His father is also called [[Nikolay Todorov (footballer, born 1964)|Nikolay Todorov]] (born 1964), who was also a professional footballer and playing for the national team of Bulgaria.<ref name=ОтПлевен/>

On 1 February 2019 he married his Scottish girlfriend Jennifer Clark in a small ceremony.<ref>[https://tech2.org/bulgaria/nikolay-todorov-passed-under-marriage/ Nikolay Todorov passed under marriage]</ref>

'''Sean Mackie''' (born 4 November 1998) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]]. Mackie has previously played for [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]], [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] and [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].

==Career==
===Club===
Mackie joined [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] in 2015 from the Fife Elite Academy, signing a two-year contract.<ref name = "raith">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35672843 |title=Hibernian move for Raith Rovers teenager Mackie |website=BBC Sport |date=26 February 2016 |accessdate=27 April 2017}}</ref> He made one first team appearance for Raith before moving to [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in February 2016.<ref name = "raith"/> Hibs paid a fee of £25,000 for the player.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-complete-signing-of-sean-mackie-1-4038863 |title=Hibs complete signing of Sean Mackie |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=26 February 2016 |accessdate=27 April 2017}}</ref>

Mackie was loaned to [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]] for the first part of the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/6623 |title=Mackie and Stirling join Berwick on loan |website=Hibernian FC |date=8 July 2016 |accessdate=27 April 2017}}</ref> He made his first team debut for Hibs in April 2017, in a 3–2 win against Raith Rovers.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-3-raith-2-keatings-free-kick-wins-it-at-the-death-1-4430650 |title=Hibs 3, Raith 2: Keatings free-kick wins it at the death |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |first=Anthony |last=Brown |date=26 April 2017 |accessdate=6 July 2017}}</ref> On 6 July 2017, Mackie joined [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] on a six-month development loan deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/7648 |title=Allan and Mackie join Edinburgh City on loan |website=Hibernian FC |date=6 July 2017 |accessdate=6 July 2017}}</ref>

In July 2019, Mackie signed an extended contract with Hibs.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/10107 |title=SEAN MACKIE AGREES CONTRACT EXTENSION |website=Hibernian FC |date=5 July 2019 |accessdate=5 July 2019}}</ref> In September 2019, Mackie joined [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on loan.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49559988 |title=Jason Naismith signs season loan at Hibernian from Peterborough |website=BBC Sport |date=3 September 2019 |accessdate=3 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49582563 |title=Sean Mackie: Hibs defender aims to boost prospects at Dundee |first=Tyrone |last=Smith |website=BBC Sport |date=4 September 2019 |accessdate=4 September 2019}}</ref> This arrangement was curtailed in January 2020 due to Mackie suffering an injury.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/frustration-for-dee-as-mullen-and-murray-moves-hit-buffers/amp/ |title=Frustration for Dee as Mullen and Murray moves hit buffers |first=George |last=Cran |newspaper=Evening Telegraph |date=31 January 2020 |accessdate=3 February 2020}}</ref>

Mackie continued to suffer from injury problems over the next two seasons, limiting his appearances for Hibs. With his contract due to expire at the end of the 2021–22 season, he was loaned to former club Raith Rovers in February 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/sean-mackie-joins-raith-rovers-on-loan |title=Sean Mackie Joins Raith Rovers On Loan |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=12 February 2022 |accessdate=12 February 2022}}</ref> While with Raith, Mackie would win the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]].<ref name="BBC Sport">{{Cite news |title=Raith beat Queens to claim SPFL Trust Trophy |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60902630 |access-date=2022-06-06}}</ref> He was released by Hibs in June 2022, at the end of his contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61675106 |title=Hibernian: Scott Allan, Alex Gogic, Drey Wright and Jamie Murphy among six exits |website=BBC Sport |date=2 June 2022 |accessdate=2 June 2022}}</ref>

On 9 June 2022, Mackie was signed by [[Scottish League One]] side [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=McGinn teams up with former Hibs team-mate as he completes Falkirk switch |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/mcginn-teams-up-with-ex-hibs-team-mate-as-he-completes-falkirk-switch-3726097 |website=www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com|date=9 June 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=SEAN MACKIE JOINS THE BAIRNS! |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2022/06/09/sean-mackie-joins-the-bairns/ |access-date=2022-06-09 |website=Falkirk Football Club |date=9 June 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref> In March 2024, Mackie won the [[2023–24 Scottish League One|League One title]] with the ''Bairns'' on the same night they destroyed [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] at [[Links Park]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |title=Falkirk crowned champions prior to rampant victory |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68644141 |access-date=2024-03-31 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> After completing an unbeaten league season with Falkirk, Mackie signed an extension with the ''Bairns'' to keep him there for the following season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-15 |title=SEAN MACKIE PENS NEW DEAL - Falkirk Football Club |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2024/05/15/sean-mackie-pens-new-deal/ |access-date=2024-05-20 |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 20 July 2024, Mackie scored his first goal for Falkirk in a [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage win over [[Buckie Thistle F.C.|Buckie Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buckie Thistle vs Falkirk: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cv2gj24rylpt |access-date=2024-07-20 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Two weeks later, he netted his first league goal in Falkirk's first game back in the [[Scottish Championship]], scoring the winning goal against [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Winning start for Falkirk {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/winning-start-for-falkirk |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> On 2 May 2025, Mackie started in a 3–1 home win over [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] which confirmed him and Falkirk as back-to-back league title winners, as well as their promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Falkirk beat Hamilton Academical 3-1 to win Scottish Championship title and promotion |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cj9egnedlgxt |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Mackie joined [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on 30 September 2025 on loan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sean Mackie joins Ross County on loan |website=Falkirk FC |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2025/09/30/sean-mackie-joins-ross-county-on-loan/ |date=30 September 2025 |access-date=30 September 2025}}</ref> After County's relegation to [[Scottish League One|League One]], Mackie's loan ended and Falkirk announced he was leaving them as his contract had expired.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hainey |first=Paddy |date=2026-05-22 |title=SQUAD UPDATE |url=https://falkirkfc.co.uk/squad-update-4/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=Falkirk FC |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 18 July 2026, Mackie joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 July 2026 |title=𝐌𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐢𝐞 𝐢𝐬 𝐚 𝐋𝐢𝐜𝐡𝐭𝐢𝐞! |url=https://www.facebook.com/ArbroathFootballClub/posts/%F0%9D%90%8C%F0%9D%90%9A%F0%9D%90%9C%F0%9D%90%A4%F0%9D%90%A2%F0%9D%90%9E-%F0%9D%90%A2%F0%9D%90%AC-%F0%9D%90%9A-%F0%9D%90%8B%F0%9D%90%A2%F0%9D%90%9C%F0%9D%90%A1%F0%9D%90%AD%F0%9D%90%A2%F0%9D%90%9Earbroath-football-club-are-delighted-to-announce-the-signing-/1799987681481520/ |access-date=24 August 2026 |website=facebook.com}}</ref>
===International===
Mackie made one appearance for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21 team]], in March 2019.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/four-players-from-hearts-and-hibs-included-in-scotland-under-21-squad-1-4882883 |title=Four players from Hearts and Hibs included in Scotland Under-21 squad |work=Edinburgh Evening News |date=4 March 2019 |accessdate=9 March 2019 |first=Peter |last=Wales}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47697925 |title=Scotland U21 1-2 Sweden U21: Barry McGuire goal not enough |publisher=BBC Sport |date=25 March 2019|access-date=25 March 2019 }}</ref>

'''Callum Smith''' (born 13 November 1999) is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]]<ref name="DAFC profile">{{cite web|title=U20s squad – Callum Smith |url=http://dafc.co.uk/people.php?SID=U20s&ID=80 |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |accessdate=29 April 2017}}</ref> professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]]. Smith has previously played for [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]], [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]], [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] and [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].

==Career==
Smith was educated at [[Beath High School]] and began his career with [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]]'s youth squad, before moving to [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], nicknamed ''the Pars'', to join the Under 15s side.<ref name="DAFC profile"/> Smith then continued his development with the Fife Elite Football Academy, after the amalgamation of [[Fife]]'s football clubs' youth sides into one academy. In 2016, Smith returned to the Pars, signing a one-year contract with the club to play for the side's development squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Two more for U20s |url=http://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Two_more_for_under_20s&ID=9303 |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=20 May 2016 |accessdate=29 April 2017}}</ref> His first appearance for the first-team came in the [[Scottish League Cup]], where he came on as a 78th-minute substitute for [[Michael Moffat]] in the 5–1 loss to [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] at [[East End Park]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dunfermline 1 – 5 Inverness CT |url=http://spfl.co.uk/league-cup/fixture/3637857/ |publisher=Scottish Professional Football League |date=26 July 2016 |accessdate=29 April 2017 |archive-date=16 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170816003555/https://spfl.co.uk/league-cup/fixture/3637857/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Smith impressed with his performances for the youth side, becoming the club's top scorer in the [[SPFL Development League]],{{citation needed|date=April 2017}} which resulted in him making his first [[Scottish Championship|league]] appearance against [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref name="Morton">{{cite web|title=Dunfermline 3 Morton 1 |url=http://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Dunfermline_3_Morton_1&ID=9961 |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=29 April 2017 |accessdate=29 April 2017}}</ref> Smith replaced [[Nicky Clark]] in the 82nd minute, and made an immediate impact, setting up [[Rhys McCabe]], assisting in Dunfermline's third goal.<ref name="Morton"/>

With the club deciding not to participate in the [[2017–18 SPFL Development League]], Smith was promoted to the first team for the 2017–18 season. He played in all four Scottish League Cup group stage matches, scoring his first goal for the Pars in a 6–0 win against [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40619929 |title=Dunfermline 6–0 Elgin City |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=15 July 2017 |accessdate=1 August 2017}}</ref> His full debut came in the final match of the group stage against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] at [[Tynecastle Stadium|Tynecastle]]. With main striker [[Nicky Clark]] injured, Smith started alongside [[Declan McManus]], who he provided an assist for to put the Pars 2–1 ahead.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40760158 |title=Hearts 2–2 Dunfermline (1–3 pens) |first=Tom |last=English |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=29 July 2017 |accessdate=1 August 2017}}</ref> Smith joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] on loan at the end of January 2018,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/15912841.Pars_loan_Smith_to_Wasps/ |title=Dunfermline Athletic's Callum Smith joins Alloa Athletic on loan until the end of the season |first=Ross |last=Hart |work=Dunfermline Press |date=1 February 2018 |accessdate=9 May 2018}}</ref> helping the side to a third-place finish and victory in the [[2017–18 Scottish Championship#Championship play-offs|Championship play-offs]] over [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44020139 |title=Dumbarton 0–2 Alloa Athletic (agg 1–2) |first=Martin |last=Dowden |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=13 May 2018 |accessdate=14 May 2018 |archive-date=5 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180805125454/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44020139 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In August 2018, Smith joined League One club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on a season long loan;<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/2018/08/callum-smith/ |title=Loan Signing – Callum Smith |publisher=Arbroath FC |accessdate=24 August 2018}}</ref> despite being sidelined for two months with an injury, he made nine appearances before his loan was cut short in January 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/2019/01/callum-smith-2/ |title=Callum Smith |publisher=Arbroath FC |date=3 January 2019 |accessdate=3 January 2019}}</ref> At the beginning of the 2019–20 season, Smith moved on a season-long loan to [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] as part of a deal that saw Josh Edwards sign for Dunfermline.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49008717 |title=Josh Edwards: Dunfermline pay undisclosed fee for Airdrieonians left-back |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=16 July 2019 |accessdate=16 July 2019}}</ref>

Smith left Dunfermline after the curtailed 2019–20 season, and signed a two-year contract with [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] in June 2020.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/hamilton-bring-striker-first-summer-22199511 |title=Hamilton bring striker in as first summer signing |first=Andy |last=McGilvray |newspaper=Daily Record |date=16 June 2020 |accessdate=25 June 2020}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Hamilton in a 3–0 win over [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on 2 January 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55450351 |title=Hamilton 3–0 Motherwell |date=2 January 2020 |publisher=BBC|accessdate=2 January 2020}}</ref>

He joined Airdrieonians on 5 August 2021, and helped them win promotion to the [[Scottish Championship|Championship]] in 2022–23.<ref name = raith/>

[[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] signed Smith on a two-year contract in June 2023.<ref name = raith>{{cite web |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/62006/callum-smith-signs-for-the-rovers.htm |title=Callum Smith signs for The Rovers |publisher=Raith Rovers FC |date=6 June 2023 |accessdate=7 June 2023}}</ref>

On 3 January 2026, Smith signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/callum-smith-queens-park-sean-crighton-signing/|title=Sean Crighton welcomes First new signing to Lochinch|publisher=[[Queen's Park F.C.]]|date=3 January 2026|accessdate=16 January 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Smith's younger brother [[Connor Smith (footballer, born 2002)|Connor]] is also a footballer<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.deadlinenews.co.uk/2017/08/17/dunfermline-youngster-callum-smith-pinching-scotland-call/|title=Dunfermline youngster Callum Smith pinching himself after Scotland call-up|date=17 August 2017|accessdate=21 May 2018|author=Iain Collin|publisher=Deadline News}}</ref> – they came up against one another in the [[Scottish Championship]] Promotion play-off final in both the [[2021–22 Scottish Championship#Championship play-offs|2021–22]] (Queen's Park, with Connor on loan and among the scorers, defeated Callum's Airdrie)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.airdriefc.com/results21-22/220515 |title=Airdrieonians 1–2 Queen's Park |date=15 May 2022|accessdate=20 May 2023|website=Airdrieonians FC}}</ref> and [[2022–23 Scottish Championship#Championship play-offs|2022–23 seasons]] (Airdrie overcame Hamilton aided by a goal from Callum in the first leg against his former club;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/airdrie-goal-hero-callum-smith-30011145 |title=Airdrie goal hero Callum Smith silenced jeering Hamilton Accies fans with 'important' goal|date=19 May 2023|accessdate=20 May 2023|author=Andy McGilvray|website=Daily Record}}</ref> Connor levelled the tie for the opposition in the return, and the outcome was settled on penalties).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65579896|title=Hamilton Academical 2-1 Airdrieonians (agg 2-2): Visitors promoted after penalty shoot-out|date=20 May 2023|accessdate=20 May 2023|website=BBC Sport|author=Clive Lindsay}}</ref>

'''Stuart Morrison''' (born 18 April 1999) is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|centre back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]]. Morrison has previously played for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]], [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] and [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]]. Morrison has also represented [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] at [[Scotland national under-19 football team|U19 level]].<ref name="CT Connection">{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Morrison%E2%80%99s_Caley_Thistle_connection&ID=11224 |title=Morrison's Caley Thistle connection |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=25 May 2019 |accessdate=25 May 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
Morrison, who attended [[Inverkeithing High School]], started his career with [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]'s youth academy from the age of eight years old.<ref name="CT Connection"/> Morrison was then with Fife's Elite Football Academy before re-signing with the Pars in May 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Stuart_Morrison_signs_from_Fife_Elite&ID=9277 |title=Stuart Morrison signs from Fife Elite |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=1 May 2016 |accessdate=26 May 2019}}</ref> Morrison was then sent out on loan to [[Scottish League Two]] club [[F.C. Edinburgh|Edinburgh]], where he spent the [[2017–18 in Scottish football|2017-18]] season,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.edinburghcityfc.com/2017/08/11/welcome-stuart-morrison/ |title=Welcome Stuart Morrison! |publisher=Edinburgh City FC |date=11 August 2017 |accessdate=25 May 2019}}</ref> where he played 23 times for the ''Citizens''.

For the majority of the [[2018–19 in Scottish football|2018-19]] season, Morrison was playing with the ''Pars'' [[SPFL Reserve League|reserve]] team, although he was also an unused substitute for a number of first-team matches.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://us.soccerway.com/players/stuart-morrison/474692/ |title=S. Morrison |publisher=Soccerway |accessdate=25 May 2019}}</ref> On 14 August 2018, Morrison debuted for the first-team in a [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] match versus [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], his boyhood club that he supported, where he played the entire match in a 2–1 away win.<ref name="CT Connection"/> Morrison had his league debut, also against the ''Caley Jags'' on the final day of the 2018–19 season.<ref name="CT Connection"/> Morrison then signed a new one-year deal with the Pars in May 2019. In February 2020, Morrison signed on loan with [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] until the end of the [[2019-20 in Scottish football|2019-20]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Stuart_Morrison_out_on_loan&ID=11715 |title=Stuart Morrison out on loan |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=2 February 2020 |accessdate=11 August 2020}}</ref> In June 2020, Morrison was released by the Pars at the end of his contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Morrison_pens_new_deal&ID=11243 |title=Stuart Morrison pens new deal |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=24 May 2019 |accessdate=26 May 2019}}</ref>

On 11 August 2020, Morrison signed a permanent deal with [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/stuart-morrison-returns/ |title=Stuart Morrison returns |publisher=Queen's Park FC |date=11 August 2020 |accessdate=11 August 2020}}</ref>

On 31 May 2022, Morrison signed a one-year contract with [[Scottish League One]] club [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://qosfc.com/news-5774 | title=QosFC: Welcome Stuart Morrison }}</ref>

On 9 June 2023, Morrison signed a one-year contract with [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]].<ref>https://forfarathletic.co.uk/item/5446-fourth-close-season-signing-confirmed</ref>

On 13 June 2026, Morrison signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Morrison makes the move |url=https://x.com/ArbroathFC/status/2065827269570867367 |access-date=17 October 2026 |work=Arbroath FC |date=13 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Scott Alexander Stewart''' (born 29 April 1996) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|full-back]] or [[midfielder]]. He began his career at [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].

==Career==
===Airdrieonians===
Stewart was born in [[Edinburgh]] but raised in [[Rutherglen]], [[South Lanarkshire]] where he attended [[Stonelaw High School]].<ref name=dad2/><ref name=dad/> His father [[Sandy Stewart (footballer)|Sandy]] was a footballer who spent the majority of his career with [[Airdrieonians F.C. (1878)|the original Airdrieonians club]] and also served as player and manager at its successor [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrie United]],<ref name=dad2/> where Scott began his career in the youth setup.<ref name=dad/>

At the age of 17, Stewart received his first call-up to the senior squad at the club (now renamed Airdrieonians) in August 2013,<ref name=sway/> making his senior debut two months later in a 2–0 home defeat to [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] in [[Scottish League One]], with his first start in the competition against [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]] in March 2014.<ref name=dad>{{cite news|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/scott-stewart-dedicates-first-career-3340937|title=Scott Stewart dedicates first career start to Airdrieonians legend dad Sandy|work=Daily Record|date=2 April 2014|accessdate=23 July 2019}}</ref> He initially began his career as a [[midfielder]] but retrained as a full-back, which he stated drew more scrutiny on his performances from his father, who had played the same position.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/airdrieonians-v-east-fife-scott-8833779|title=Airdrieonians v East Fife: Scott Stewart wants to prove he's chip off the old block|work=Daily Record|date=17 September 2016|accessdate=23 July 2019}}</ref> After three seasons as a squad member, he became a regular starter for the ''Diamonds'' in the [[2016–17 in Scottish football|2016–17 campaign]], going on to make over 100 appearances over the next three years,<ref name=sway/><ref>[https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=72470 Scott Stewart], Soccerbase</ref> including a [[2016–17 Scottish Championship#Championship play-offs|promotion playoff semi-final defeat]] to [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] on penalties in 2017<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39833667 Alloa Athletic 1–0 Airdrieonians], BBC Sport, 13 May 2017</ref> (the closest Airdrie came to either being promoted or relegated in his time with the club) and a [[Scottish Cup]] visit to holders [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2019.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46847909 Celtic 3–0 Airdrieonians], BBC Sport, 19 January 2019</ref>

He was voted the Airdrieonians 'Young Player of the Year' for 2016–17<ref name=poy/> and the overall 'Player of the Year' for 2017–18,<ref name=poy>[https://www.airdriefc.com/player-of-the-year Player of the Year], Airdrieonians FC</ref> having been named [[Captain (association football)|team captain]] in the latter part of that season<ref>[https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/airdrieonians-captain-scott-stewart-calls-11934626 Airdrieonians captain Scott Stewart calls for players to turn draws into wins for play-off push], Daily Record, 2 February 2018</ref> and agreed a new contract to stay at the club.<ref name=snap>[https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/airdrieonians-snap-up-scott-stewart-12092625 Airdrieonians snap up Scott Stewart on new deal in signing 'coup' as clubs track star], Daily Record, 28 February 2018</ref>

===Arbroath===
In June 2019, Stewart transferred to [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]], newly promoted to the [[Scottish Championship]].<ref>[http://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/2019/06/scott-stewart/ New signing – Scott Stewart], Arbroath FC, 3 June 2019</ref> He made his debut for the club on 23 July 2019, in a 3–0 defeat away to [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in the [[2019–20 Scottish League Cup group stage#Group C|group stage]] of the [[2019–20 Scottish League Cup]].<ref>[https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/latest-hibs-news/hibs-3-arbroath-0-hibs-are-convincing-winners-in-the-betfred-cup-1-4970132 Hibs 3, Arbroath 0. Hibs are convincing winners in the Betfred Cup], ''Edinburgh Evening News'', 23 July 2019</ref> He was an important member of the ''Red Lichties'' team in their bid for promotion to the [[Scottish Premiership]] in the [[2021–22 Scottish Championship|2021–22 season]], while also working as a [[Physical Education|P.E.]] teacher at Rutherglen's [[Trinity High School, Rutherglen|Trinity High School]].<ref>[https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/inside-arbroath-fairytale-scott-stewart-26149882 Inside the Arbroath fairytale as Scott Stewart says Dick Campbell is keeping top flight talk to a minimum], Scott McDermott, '' Daily Record'', 6 February 2022</ref><ref>[https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/3196856/arbroath-ace-scott-stewart-pupil-jibes/ PE teacher Arbroath ace Scott Stewart reveals bid to turn post-holiday pupil jibes into adulation], Scott Lorimer, ''The Courier'', 14 April 2022</ref> The club narrowly avoided relegation in [[2022–23 Arbroath F.C. season|2022–23]] but finished bottom of the division in [[2023–24 Arbroath F.C. season|2023–24]]. They bounced back immediately as winners of [[2024–25 Scottish League One]],<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ce3v4jqxjjqt Arbroath 4-0 Stenhousemuir - Scottish League One], ''BBC Sport'', 12 April 2025</ref> with Stewart named in the Team of the Season.

'''Andrew Winter''' (born 10 March 2002) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{soccerbase|118954}}</ref>

==Club career==
Winter began his career with [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/accies-kids-right-path-because-20621664|title=Accies kids are on the right path because boss believes in them, says Academy director George Cairns|first=Andy|last=McGilvray|date=19 October 2019|website=Daily Record}}</ref> joining the club aged 10.<ref name=shine>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/winter-hopes-shine-field-despite-seeing-referee-dad-criticised-past|title=Winter hopes to shine on field despite seeing referee dad criticised in the past|author1=FourFourTwo Staff|date=17 January 2020|website=fourfourtwo.com}}</ref><ref name=ready>https://www.hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/andrew-winter-insists-he-will-be-ready-when-accies-chance-comes/</ref> He played and scored in the [[UEFA Youth League]]<ref name=fcb22>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/hamilton-accies-uefa-youth-league-13475206|title=Hamilton Accies UEFA Youth League adventure continues after dramatic penalty victory over Basel|work=Daily Record|date=24 October 2018|accessdate=25 October 2018}}</ref> and the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bscglasgow.co.uk/event/hamilton-academical-reserves-vs-bsc-glasgow/|title=Hamilton Academical Reserves vs BSC Glasgow|newspaper=BSC Glasgow |date=7 August 2019}}</ref> with the ''Accies'' underage teams before making his senior debut on 18 January 2020, a 5–0 win over [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] in the [[2019–20 Scottish Cup]] fourth round in which he entered as a substitute and scored the fourth goal.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51073238|title=Hamilton 5–0 Edinburgh City: Debut goals for Dales and Winter|work=BBC Sport |date=18 January 2020}}</ref> He then made his first [[Scottish Premiership]] appearance the following week, again coming off the bench in a 4–2 defeat away to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]]. His first start soon followed in the Scottish Cup, playing the entirety of a 4–1 home defeat for Hamilton at the hands of [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51337079|title=Hamilton Academical 1–4 Rangers: Visitors book Scottish Cup quarter-final berth|work=BBC Sport |date=8 February 2020}}</ref>

Winter was released from [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] in May 2024.  The following month, he began training with [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Former Hamilton Accies striker Andy Winter training with Livingston|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/former-hamilton-accies-striker-andy-33050033|work=Daily Record|date=17 June 2024}}</ref> He signed a one-year deal with Livi in July 2024.<ref>{{cite news|title=A Summer signing with a Winter feel to it|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/a-summer-signing-with-a-winter-feel-to-it/|website=livingstonfc.co.uk|date=10 July 2024}}</ref>

In January 2025, Winter signed for [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on loan for the remainder of the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Andy Winter joins Arbroath on loan|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/andy-winter-joins-arbroath-on-loan/|website=livingstonfc.co.uk|date=24 January 2025}}</ref> He joined [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on loan in January 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/squad-update-andy-winter-goes-on-loan-to-raith-rovers/|title=Squad Update | Andy Winter goes on loan to Raith Rovers|first=Dave|last=Black|date=2 January 2026}}</ref>

He left Livingston in May 2026 following the expiration of his contract,<ref>{{cite web |title=Squad Update – Retained & Released List|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/squad-update-retained-released-list/|website=livingstonfc.co.uk|date=19 May 2026}}</ref> and signed a one-year deal with Arbroath on 5 June.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 June 2026 |title=𝐖𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐑𝐞𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐧𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐆𝐚𝐲𝐟𝐢𝐞𝐥𝐝! |url=https://x.com/ArbroathFC/status/2062928838191874191 |access-date=8 July 2026 |website=Arbroath FC on X}}</ref>

==International career==
He has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]], [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Scotland national under-18 football team|under-18]] youth levels.<ref>{{SFA player|286188}}</ref>

'''David Gold''' (born 1 January 1993) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]], where he is also co-manager.<ref>{{soccerbase|70929}}</ref>

He has previously played for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/20130914/gold-joins-queens-park-on-loan_2262950_3457920 |title=Gold Joins Queen's Park on Loan |work=www.hibernianfc.co.uk |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=14 September 2013 |accessdate=10 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140531191243/http://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/20130914/gold-joins-queens-park-on-loan_2262950_3457920 |archive-date=31 May 2014}}</ref> [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cowdenbeathfc.com/index.php?act=viewNews&id=1466 |title=First Signing Arrives |work=www.cowdenbeathfc.com |publisher=Cowdenbeath FC |date=9 January 2014 |accessdate=10 February 2020}}</ref> and [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.berwickshirenews.co.uk/sport/football/berwick-rangers/david-gold-is-latest-addition-to-berwick-squad-1-3468483 | title=David Gold is latest addition to Berwick squad |newspaper=Berwickshire News  | date=7 July 2014 | accessdate=10 February 2020}}</ref>

He took interim charge of Arbroath alongside [[Colin Hamilton (footballer)|Colin Hamilton]] in August 2024, become becoming permanent player-manager in September 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cql3lz1plv7o|title=Hamilton and Gold confirmed as new Arbroath player-managers|date=12 September 2024|website=BBC}}</ref>
