'''Michael McKenna''' (born 4 January 1991) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].

==Career==
Born in [[Edinburgh]],<ref name="worldfootball">{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe365181/michael-mckenna/ |title=Michael McKenna |website=worldfootball.net |publisher=HEIM:SPIEL |access-date=25 April 2020}}</ref> McKenna spent time in [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]]'s youth academy<ref name="courier1">{{Cite news |url=https://www.eastlothiancourier.com/sport/13562584.musselburgh-winger-michael-earns-dream-move-to-spfl-championship/ |title=Musselburgh winger Michael earns dream move to SPFL Championship |date=11 July 2014 |work=East Lothian Courier |access-date=25 April 2020 |language=en}}</ref> before joining [[Musselburgh Athletic F.C.|Musselburgh Athletic]] in 2012.<ref name="worldfootball" /> In the summer of 2014, McKenna signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on a one-year contract.<ref name="courier1" /> In summer 2015, McKenna joined [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/berwick-make-first-summer-signings |title=Berwick make first summer signings |date=5 June 2015 |website=spfl.co.uk |access-date=25 April 2020}}</ref> Having already signed a pre-contract agreement with the club, McKenna signed for [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] for an undisclosed fee in January 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.berwick-advertiser.co.uk/news/mckenna-joins-arbroath-409852 |title=McKenna joins Arbroath |date=30 January 2018 |work=Berwick Advertiser |access-date=25 April 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

On the expiration of his contract with Arbroath in May 2024, McKenna signed a one-year contract with [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref name="MICHAEL MCKENNA JOINS FALKIRK">{{Cite web |date=2024-05-07 |title=MICHAEL MCKENNA JOINS FALKIRK |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2024/05/07/michael-mckenna-joins-falkirk/}}</ref>

He left [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] in January 2025 and joined [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] on a two-and-a-half year deal, reuniting him with former boss [[Dick Campbell (footballer, born 1953)|Dick Campbell]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://eastfifefc.info/latest-news/1806-mckenna-signs-on |title=McKenna signs on |website=East Fife FC |date=30 January 2025 |accessdate=5 February 2025}}</ref>

On 13 June 2026, McKenna rejoined former club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mikey returns to Gayfield |url=https://x.com/ArbroathFC/status/2065873921614688298 |access-date=17 October 2026 |work=Arbroath FC |date=13 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Scott McGill''' (born 27 January 2002) is a Scottish professional  [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]]. He has previously played for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]], [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]], [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] and [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]].

==Early and personal life==
Born in [[Edinburgh]],<ref name="sw">{{Cite web |title=S. McGill |url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/scott-mcgill/622257/ |access-date=26 March 2021 |website=Soccerway}}</ref> McGill grew up in [[Gorgie|Chesser]] and attended Balgreen primary school, thereafter joining the SFA Performance Program at Broughton High school Edinburgh.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Anderson |first=Barry |date=12 November 2020 |title=Revealed: The Gorgie life of Hearts teenager Scott McGill |language=en |work=Edinburgh Evening News |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/revealed-gorgie-life-hearts-teenager-scott-mcgill-3032559 |access-date=21 April 2021}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Scott McGill |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/squads/academy/academy-team/scott-mcgill |access-date=21 July 2021 |website=heartsfc.co.uk |publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C.}}</ref>

==Career==
===Hearts===
McGill played youth football for [[Lothian Thistle Hutchison Vale F.C.|Hutchison Vale]] and [[Tynecastle F.C.|Tynecastle]] and later for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref name="auto" /> He signed his first professional contract with the club in June 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 June 2018 |title=Nine make step up |url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/nine-make-step-up |access-date=21 July 2021 |website=heartsfc.co.uk |publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C.}}</ref> He made his debut for Heart of Midlothian on 10 October 2020 in a 1–0 [[Scottish League Cup]] victory over [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Atkinson |first=Mark |date=11 October 2020 |title=Hearts boss Robbie Neilson explains how Scott McGill caught his eye and assesses his appearance for club |work=Edinburgh Evening News |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-boss-robbie-neilson-explains-how-scott-mcgill-caught-his-eye-and-assesses-his-appearance-club-2999738 |access-date=21 July 2021}}</ref> and appeared again for them three days later in a 3–1 League Cup victory over [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sked |first=Joel |date=13 October 2020 |title=How the Hearts players rated in the 3–1 win over Raith Rovers to make it three wins from three in the Betfred Cup |work=Edinburgh Evening News |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/how-hearts-players-rated-3-1-win-over-raith-rovers-make-it-three-wins-three-betfred-cup-3002416 |access-date=21 July 2021}}</ref><ref name="sw" /> McGill played 90 minutes in a 3-2 victory over East Fife in November 2020 in the Scottish League Cup.

He made his league debut for Hearts on 20 April 2021 in a goalless draw with [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref name="sw" /> Scott made four appearances for Heart of Midlothian.

===Airdrieonians===

On 21 July 2021, he joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] on loan until May 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Robertson |first=Euan |date=21 July 2021 |title=Hearts youngster Scott McGill joins Airdrie on-loan in bid for regular football |language=en |work=EdinburghLive |url=https://www.edinburghlive.co.uk/sport/football/hearts-youngster-scott-mcgill-joins-21112432 |access-date=21 July 2021}}</ref> McGill scored on his debut for Airdrieonians in a 2–0 win in the League Cup against their [[Lanarkshire derby]] rivals [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/deadly-double-gives-airdrieonians-first-win-over-motherwell-in-20-years-nxzfc05qv |title=Deadly double gives Airdrieonians first win over Motherwell in 20 years |first=Alison |last=McConnell |newspaper=[[The Times]] |date=21 July 2021 |access-date=24 July 2021}}</ref> He went on to play 41 times and score 1 league cup goal and 4 league goals for Airdrieonians during the [[2021–22 Scottish League One]] season.<ref name="sb2122"/>

===Kelty Hearts===

McGill was loaned to [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] in August 2022.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/3589066/kelty-hearts-add-to-midfield-by-bringing-in-loan-signing-from-premiership-side/ |title=Kelty Hearts add to midfield by bringing in loan signing from Premiership side |newspaper=The Courier |first=Craig |last=Cairns |date=12 August 2022 |accessdate=13 August 2022}}</ref> He would make 13 appearances and would score 1 goal in a 2-0 league victory against Falkirk. McGill returned to his parent club Hearts in January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Phil |date=12 January 2023 |title=Hearts duo Scott McGill and Cammy Logan return from loan spell at Kelty Hearts |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-duo-scott-mcgill-and-cammy-logan-return-from-loan-spell-at-kelty-hearts-3984150 |access-date=13 January 2023 |website=edinburghnews.scotsman.com}}</ref> Later that month, he would join [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Players {{!}} Raith Rovers FC |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/players |access-date=2023-01-20 |website=www.raithrovers.net}}</ref>

===Raith Rovers===
Following a loan spell at the club, McGill signed on a permanent basis with [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] during the summer of 2023.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-midfielder-scott-mcgill-reveals-why-he-is-leaving-tynecastle-after-agreeing-a-pre-contract-deal-4152894 |title=Hearts midfielder Scott McGill reveals why he is leaving Tynecastle after agreeing a pre-contract deal |first=Barry |last=Anderson |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=22 May 2023 |accessdate=22 May 2023}}</ref>

===Dundalk===
In June 2024, McGill signed for [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] club [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] on a permanent basis, signing under manager [[Jon Daly (footballer)|Jon Daly]] a coach at Heart of Midlothian when McGill was coming through the Academy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/louth/sport/soccer/new-dundalk-fc-signing-scott-mcgill-says-he-wants-to-help-the-club-push-clear-of-the-relegation/a323527817.html|title=New Dundalk FC signing Scott McGill says he wants to help the club push clear of the relegation|work=independent.ie|publisher=[[Irish Independent]] |date=25 June 2024 |accessdate=13 July 2024}}</ref>

===Stenhousemuir===
On 15 January 2025, McGill signed an 18 month contract with [[Scottish League One]] club [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Scott McGill signs 18-month deal | date=15 January 2025 | url=https://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/2025/01/15/scott-mcgill-signs-18-month-deal/ }}</ref>After playing 58 times and helping  them gain promotion to the championship, McGill moved on to another challenge .

===Arbroath===
On 5 June 2026, McGill signed a two-year deal with [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{cite news |title=McGill joins The Lichties |url=https://x.com/ArbroathFC/status/2062852330383413548?lang=en |access-date=17 October 2026 |work=Arbroath FC |date=5 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Aidan McAdams''' (born 23 March 1999) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].

==Club career==
McAdams was born in [[Glasgow]].<ref name="sw" /> Having been at [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]'s academy from the age of 8, he switched to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in 2017 on a three-year contract.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2019/03/03/rangers-aiden-mcadams-once-of-celtic-sends-message-on-twitter/|title=Rangers' Aiden McAdams, once of Celtic, sends message on Twitter|first=Shane|last=Callaghan|date=3 March 2019|website=HITC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/17232913.kid-keeper-aidan-mcadams-eyes-loan-switch-boost-rangers-first-team-ambitions/|title=Kid keeper Aidan McAdams eyes loan switch to boost his Rangers first team ambitions|website=HeraldScotland |date=21 November 2018 }}</ref>

He joined [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]] on loan in January 2019,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsandstar.co.uk/sport/17348482.annan-athletic-sign-teenage-keeper-loan-rangers-kyle-bradley-extends-galabank-stay/|title=Annan Athletic sign teenage keeper on loan from Rangers while Kyle Bradley extends Galabank stay|website=News and Star |date=10 January 2019 }}</ref> and made his debut for them on 2 March 2019 in a 2–1 victory over [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]].<ref name="auto"/> He appeared in three matches for Annan Athletic.<ref name="soccerbase">{{soccerbase|93294}}</ref>

In August 2019, McAdams joined [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] on loan until January 2020,<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1159826902598766592 |user=RFC_Youth |title=@RFC_Youth goalkeeper Aidan McAdams has joined @EdinburghCityFC on loan until January. |author=Rangers Youth Academy |date=9 August 2019 |access-date=20 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rangersnews.uk/club-news/rangers-macadams-edinburgh-city-loan/|title=Rangers youth keeper seals short-term exit to League Two side|work=Rangers News |date=10 August 2019}}</ref> going on to play 12 times for the club.<ref name="soccerbase" /> He joined Northern Irish side [[Portadown F.C.|Portadown]] on loan in January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://portadownfc.co.uk/player/aidan-mcadams/|title=Aidan McAdams|access-date=20 October 2020|archive-date=24 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024124958/https://portadownfc.co.uk/player/aidan-mcadams/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was released by Rangers at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rangers.co.uk/article/five-to-depart-academy-2/56BgFNFYSXR49BcAQSLnyQ|title=Five To Depart Academy|website=www.rangers.co.uk}}</ref>

McAdams joined [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] in September 2020 on a season-long deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gmfc.net/new-ton-boys-sign-on/|title=New 'Ton Boys Sign On|date=17 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/sport/18769084.ex-celtic-rangers-youngster-mcadams-says-lower-league-experience-will-help-morton/|title=Ex-Celtic and Rangers youngster McAdams says lower league experience will help him at Morton|website=Greenock Telegraph |date=4 October 2020 }}</ref>

He moved to [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in June 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/new-ayr-united-goalkeeper-aidan-24365836|title = Ayr United goalie Aidan McAdams: Why I had to follow David Hopkin to Somerset|date = 21 June 2021}}</ref>

McAdams would have brief stints with [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]] and Northern Irish side [[Larne F.C.|Larne]], winning the [[NIFL Premiership]] while with the latter.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 August 2023 |title=@EdinburghCityFC on X |url=https://x.com/EdinburghCityFC/status/1692635325645152374 |access-date=17 July 2024 |website=x.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-03 |title=McAdams arrives as first January signing {{!}} Larne FC |url=https://larnefc.com/mcadams-arrives-as-first-january-signing/ |access-date=2024-07-17 |website=larnefc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

On 13 July 2024, McAdams signed for [[Scottish League One]] club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arbroath Football Club - Official |date=13 July 2024 |title=𝐌𝐜𝐀𝐝𝐚𝐦𝐬 𝐓𝐨 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐲 𝐈𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐨𝐨𝐧! |url=https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=1150145703132391&set=a.1212492825436611 |access-date=2024-07-17 |website=www.facebook.com}}</ref>

==International career==
He has represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-15 football team|under-15]], [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]], [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] levels.<ref>{{SFA player|167131}}</ref>

'''Dylan Reid''' (born 1 March 2005) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} side [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]]. He was the youngest player in [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]'s history to make a competitive appearance.

==Club career==

===St Mirren===

Reid made his professional debut for [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] aged 16 years and six days, coming off the bench in the 88th minute of a 3–0 [[Scottish Premiership]] defeat against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]. He became the youngest debutant in St Mirren's history.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56219996|title=Rangers a point from title after victory|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> Shortly after this, Reid reportedly attracted interest from [[Bundesliga]] giants [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] who were interested in signing him for their academy and had brought him over to visit their facilities. However, Reid declined the offer and decided to stay at St Mirren.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-08 |title=St Mirren planning underway for next season as Jim Goodwin takes pride in academy progress |url=https://www.nottheoldfirm.com/interview/st-mirren-planning-underway-for-next-season-as-jim-goodwin-takes-pride-in-academy-progress/ |access-date=2023-01-08 |website=Not The Old Firm |language=en-GB}}</ref> He also garnered interest earlier in his youth career from [[Primeira Liga]] side [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] and had a trial period with them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robertson |first=Euan |date=2022-05-10 |title=Dylan Reid 'targeted' for Benfica transfer with Saints kid on Bayern Munich list |url=https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/dylan-reid-targeted-benfica-transfer-23916793 |access-date=2023-01-08 |website=footballscotland |language=en}}</ref>

In March 2021, Reid signed a new contract with St Mirren lasting until summer 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/3937-dylan-reid-agrees-contract-extension|title=DYLAN REID AGREES CONTRACT EXTENSION|publisher=[[St Mirren F.C.]]|date=19 March 2021|accessdate=20 April 2021}}</ref> In April 2021, it was announced that he would miss two weeks of action to focus on school work.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56807526|title=Dylan Reid: St Mirren midfielder misses games to focus on school|publisher=BBC Sport|date=19 April 2021|accessdate=20 April 2021}}</ref> He made his first career start in September 2021, during a 0-0 draw with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/in-your-area/renfrewshire/jim-goodwin-adamant-st-mirren-24973814|title = Goodwin adamant Saints kids will always get chance to shine as Reid impresses|date = 13 September 2021}}</ref> Following the game, St Mirren manager [[Jim Goodwin]] praised Reid but said he lacked physicality and needed to "put more weight on."<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-09-16|title=St Mirren have to 'bulk up' Dylan Reid says Jim Goodwin as he provides injury update|url=https://www.nottheoldfirm.com/interview/st-mirren-must-bulk-up-dylan-reid-says-jim-goodwin-as-he-provides-injury-update/|access-date=2021-12-30|website=Not The Old Firm|language=en-GB}}</ref>

Reid did not appear in another first team game until December 2021, when he was recalled to the squad for a game against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] due to a [[COVID-19]] outbreak in the squad.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ramage|first=Ben|date=2021-12-22|title=Covid-ravaged St Mirren side battle to well-earned point against Celtic|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/in-your-area/renfrewshire/covid-ravaged-st-mirren-side-25768364|access-date=2021-12-30|website=Daily Record|language=en}}</ref> He played the full game, which ended in a goalless draw, in central midfield. He was then loaned to [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] in February 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stmirren.com/all-news/4273-dylan-reid-joins-queen-s-park-on-loan-until-the-end-of-the-season |title=DYLAN REID JOINS QUEEN'S PARK ON LOAN UNTIL THE END OF THE SEASON |website=www.stmirren.com |date=1 February 2022 |accessdate=4 February 2022}}</ref>

In July 2022, Reid rejected a contract offer from Celtic after St Mirren accepted a bid of £125,000 for the player.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c72ej5gw9qlo | title=Dylan Reid to remain with St Mirren after talks with Celtic | date=18 July 2022 }}</ref> According to St Mirren manager [[Stephen Robinson (footballer)|Stephen Robinson]], he was earmarked as a development signing for [[Celtic 'B'|Celtic B]] but chose to remain at the club as he "backed himself" to break into the first-team at St Mirren.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Fraser |date=2022-07-23 |title=Stephen Robinson says Dylan Reid has backed himself by rejecting Celtic |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/dylan-reids-celtic-transfer-rejection-27551970 |access-date=2023-01-08 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref>

===Crystal Palace===
In February 2023, Reid moved to [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] for an undisclosed fee to join their [[Crystal Palace F.C. Under-21s and Academy|Academy]] squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64668549 |title=Dylan Reid: St Mirren midfielder joins Crystal Palace for undisclosed fee |website=BBC Sport |date=16 February 2023 |accessdate=16 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-02-16 |title=Crystal Palace Academy sign Dylan Reid |url=https://www.cpfc.co.uk/news/announcement/crystal-palace-sign-dylan-reid/ |access-date=2023-02-16 }}</ref>

===Arbroath===
On 30 September 2026, Reid signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Welcome Dylan! |url=https://x.com/ArbroathFC/status/2105334940120338845 |access-date=17 October 2026 |work=Arbroath FC |date=30 September 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
After previously representing the [[Scotland national under-16 football team]] in 2019, Reid was called up for the [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17s]] in September 2021, and captained the team against [[Wales national under-17 football team|Wales]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/in-your-area/renfrewshire/st-mirren-star-dylan-reid-24904930|title=St Mirren star Dylan Reid handed Scotland armband as teenager continues to shine|date=4 September 2021}}</ref> Reid has since also won caps for the Scottish [[Scotland national under-18 football team|under-18]] and [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] teams.

'''Brody Paterson''' (born 24 April 2001) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Arbroath}} club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].

==Career==
Born in [[Kirkcaldy]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brody Paterson |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe512747/brody-paterson/ |access-date=26 November 2022 |website=worldfootball.net |language=en}}</ref> Paterson began his playing career with [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], before moving to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]'s youth sector at the age of 12.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Gould |first=Louise |date=19 November 2021 |title=Getting to know more about the B Team: Brody Paterson |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2021/november/19/getting-to-know-more-about-the-b-team--brody-paterson/ |website=Celtic FC}}</ref> In June 2018, he signed his first professional contract with Celtic,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=4 July 2022 |title=Pools sign Paterson |url=https://www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk/news/2022/july/pools-sign-paterson/ |website=www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk}}</ref> which was then renewed in May 2020, when he penned a new three-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 May 2020 |title=Brody Paterson signs new three-year deal at Paradise |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/18149/ |access-date=26 November 2022 |website=Official Celtic Football Club Website}}</ref>

Whilst under contract with Celtic, Paterson spent time on loan at [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cairns |first=Ian |date=2 October 2020 |title=Queen's Sign Brody Paterson on Loan |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/queens-sign-brody-paterson-on-loan/ |access-date=26 November 2022 |website=Queen's Park Football Club |language=en-US}}</ref> where he won the [[2020–21 Scottish League Two]],<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite news |date=20 April 2021 |title=Queen's Park seal League Two title |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56823461 |access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> and then [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 January 2022 |title=Darren O'Dea: Attacking flair pivotal to B team education and progress |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2022/january/28/darren-o-dea--attacking-flair-pivotal-to-b-team-education-and-progress/ |access-date=26 November 2022 |website=Celtic FC}}</ref> where he reached the promotional play-offs of the [[2021–22 Scottish League One]], as the club eventually lost to Queen's Park in the final round.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/brody-paterson-targets-celtic-shop-26863252|title=Celtic youngster Brody Paterson sets his sights on summer move|first=Scott|last=Burns|date=3 May 2022|website=Daily Record}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=15 May 2022 |title=Queen's Park promoted |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/queens-park-promoted |access-date=26 November 2022 |website=SPFL}}</ref> At the end of the latter season, Paterson left Celtic after turning down an offer for a new contract extension.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sullivan |first=Joe |date=7 July 2022 |title=Ross Doohan moves to Tranmere Rovers |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2022/july/07/ross-doohan-moves-to-tranmere-rovers/ |access-date=26 November 2022 |website=Celtic FC}}</ref>

On 4 July 2022, Paterson joined English [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 July 2022 |title=Hartlepool sign winger Paterson from Celtic |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62044490 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 9 January 2023, Paterson signed for [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]] on loan for the remainder of the season, re-joining with his former manager at Hartlepool, [[Paul Hartley]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 January 2023 |title=Brody Paterson Joins Cove Rangers |url=https://coverangersfc.com/2023/01/09/brody-paterson-joins-cove-rangers/ |website=Cove Rangers FC}}</ref> At the end of the [[2022–23 Hartlepool United F.C. season|2022–23 season]], the ''[[Hartlepool Mail]]'' reported that Paterson would be allowed to leave the club permanently.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hartlepoolmail.co.uk/sport/football/hartlepool-united-open-to-exit-of-former-celtic-full-back-4155341 |title=Hartlepool United open to exit of former Celtic full-back |author=Joe Ramage |publisher=Hartlepool Mail |date=24 May 2023 |access-date=28 November 2023}}</ref> In January 2024, he signed on loan for [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk/news/2024/january/scottish-duo-leave-on-loan/ |title=Scottish duo leave on loan |publisher=Hartlepool United FC |date=18 January 2024 |accessdate=18 January 2024}}</ref> He was released by Hartlepool United at the end of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk/news/2024/april/retained-list-202324/ |title=Retained List 2023/24 |website=Hartlepool United FC |date=30 April 2024 |access-date=30 April 2024}}</ref> In June 2024, it was announced Paterson had signed for Kelty Hearts on a permanent basis.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/KeltyHeartsFC/status/1806039788635767281|title=𝐁𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐲 𝐌𝐚𝐤𝐞𝐬 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐲 𝐏𝐞𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐞𝐧𝐭 |via=Twitter|access-date=26 June 2024}}</ref>

Paterson is a [[Full back (association football)|left-back]], who can also play as a [[Winger (association football)|left winger]], and provides cover both in defensive and offensive actions.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

He has cited [[Kieran Tierney]] as his main source of inspiration.<ref name=":0" />

'''Robbie Jack Hemfrey''' (born 21 February 2002) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Wishaw]],<ref name = "SW"/> Hemfrey trained with [[SL Benfica|Benfica]]'s academy at the age of 13, whilst signed to [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/young-cambuslang-goalkeeper-trains-benfica-6767495|title=Young Cambuslang goalkeeper trains at Benfica|first=Murray|last=Spooner|date=5 November 2015|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

Hemfrey then played for [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] before signing for [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] in September 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.themillers.co.uk/news/2022/september/read--millers-add-young-stopper-to-goalkeeping-department/|title=SIGNING | Millers add young stopper to goalkeeping department|website=www.themillers.co.uk}}</ref> He made his senior debut on 18 April 2023 in a 2–2 draw against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]], appearing as a half-time substitute after an injury to [[Josh Vickers]] and being hailed as a "hero" for his performance.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/football/international-football/georgie-kelly-and-robbie-hemfrey-the-heroes-as-rotherham-united-thwart-premier-league-bound-burnley-4109466|title=Georgie Kelly and Robbie Hemfrey the heroes as Rotherham United thwart Premier League-bound Burnley |date=18 April 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/football/rotherham-united-boss-matt-taylor-hails-character-but-needs-to-sign-a-new-goalkeeper-after-no-3-robbie-hemfrey-thwarts-burnley-4109499|title=Rotherham United boss Matt Taylor hails character but needs to sign a new goalkeeper after No 3 Robbie Hemfrey thwarts Burnley |date=18 April 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/football/robbie-hemfrey-rotherham-uniteds-goalkeeping-hero-on-his-45-minute-chance-and-sacrifice-for-the-teams-goal-4110760|title=Robbie Hemfrey, Rotherham United's goalkeeping hero, on his 45-minute chance and sacrifice for the team's goal |date=20 April 2023 }}</ref>

Hemfrey left Rotherham at the end of the 2022–23 season upon the expiry of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=READ {{!}} Millers confirm retained list ahead of 2023/24 season |url=https://www.themillers.co.uk/news/2023/may/read--millers-confirm-retained-list-ahead-of-202324-season/ |access-date=2023-06-15 |website=www.themillers.co.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref>

In March 2024 he signed for [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.airdriefc.com/2324-news/240315/keeper-hemfrey-checks-in|title=Keeper Hemfrey checks in|website=airdrie}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/ex-stoke-city-keeper-signs-32365807|title=Ex-Stoke City keeper signs for Airdrie amid Josh Rae concussion woe|first=Andy|last=McGilvray|date=15 March 2024|website=Daily Record}}</ref> Later that month he won the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] with the club.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68544471|title=Airdrieonians win SPFL Trust Trophy to thwart The New Saints record|work=BBC Sport |date=23 March 2024 }}</ref>

In June 2024, Hemfrey joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arbroath Football Club – Official |date=22 June 2024 |title=𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐋𝐢𝐜𝐡𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐒𝐢𝐠𝐧 𝐇𝐞𝐦𝐟𝐫𝐞𝐲 |url=https://www.facebook.com/ArbroathFootballClub/posts/pfbid0eZNQFrUqp4KGvAcF6A53mXe9sneSY2RE9XKKEYesnLqeMNcv1qBRFnyAE1fxBCgMl |access-date=2024-07-17 |website=www.facebook.com}}</ref> On 21 September 2024, Hemfrey moved on loan to [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]] until January 2025.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Clyde|url=https://www.clydefc.co.uk/news/2024/09/loan-signing-robbie-hemfrey/|title=LOAN SIGNING: Robbie Hemfrey|date=21 September 2024|access-date=26 December 2024}}</ref>

After spending time with [[East Kilbride F.C.|East Kilbride]],<ref name="auto"/> he signed for [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]] in January 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eastfifefc.co.uk/robbie-hemfrey-joins-east-fife-on-six-month-deal/|title=Robbie Hemfrey Joins East Fife on Six-Month Deal - East Fife|date=13 January 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
He played for Scotland at [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] and [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] levels.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=259961&lid=13|title=Robbie Hemfrey | Scotland | Scottish FA|website=www.scottishfa.co.uk}}</ref>

'''Oscar MacIntyre''' (born 21 December 2004) is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] professional [[association football|footballer]] who most recently played as a [[defender (association football)|left back]] for [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]]. He has previously played for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]], and [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]].

==Club career==
===Hibernian===
MacIntyre signed for the [[Hibernian F.C. Reserves and Academy|Hibernian youth academy]] from [[The Spartans F.C.|The Spartans]] in 2019, joining up at the same time as his younger brother Jacob.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.pressreader.com/uk/the-oban-times/20190905/282265257111187 |title=Oscar signs for the Hibees |newspaper=Oban Times |date=5 September 2019 |accessdate=4 March 2023}}</ref> In April 2021, Oscar signed his first professional contract with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] and debuted for the first-team in May 2022.<ref name = spartans>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-brothers-jacob-and-oscar-macintyre-speak-on-first-team-hopes-rejection-and-family-influence-3964195 |title=Hibs brothers Jacob and Oscar MacIntyre speak on first-team hopes, rejection, and family influence |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=22 December 2022 |accessdate=4 March 2023 |first=Peter |last=Wales}}</ref> Both brothers signed long-term contracts with the ''Hibees'' in August 2022.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-tie-down-academy-brothers-jacob-and-oscar-macintyre-on-long-term-deals-3795917 |title=Hibs tie down academy brothers Jacob and Oscar MacIntyre on long-term deals |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=5 August 2022 |accessdate=4 March 2023 |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin}}</ref>

On 25 August 2023, MacIntyre was sent out on loan to [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/oscar-macintyre-joins-queen-of-the-south-on-loan |title=Oscar MacIntyre Joins Queen of the South On Loan |publisher=Hibernian FC |date=25 August 2023 |accessdate=28 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.qosfc.com/news-6179 | title=QosFC: Welcome Oscar and Toby }}</ref> In February 2024 he was loaned to [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]] for the remainder of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/oscar-macintyre-joins-annan-athletic-on-loan |title=Oscar MacIntyre Joins Annan Athletic On Loan! |publisher=Hibernian FC |website=www.hibernianfc.co.uk |date=15 February 2024 |accessdate=16 February 2024}}</ref> He returned to Queen of the South on loan for the 2024–25 season.

===Inverness Caledonian Thistle===
MacIntyre moved to [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on a permanent basis in July 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cwyrydk6w85o |title=Hibs youngster MacIntyre joins Inverness CT |website=BBC Sport |date=25 July 2025|accessdate=25 July 2025}}</ref>

On 25 May 2026 it was announced that MacIntyre was one of 9 players who would be leaving Inverness upon the expiration of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-25 |title=Caley Jags confirm release of nine players at the end of their contracts |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-jags-confirm-release-of-nine-players-at-the-end-of-the-435941/ |access-date=2026-05-31 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

==Sports family==
His younger brother [[Jacob MacIntyre]] is also a footballer, currently in the Hibernian youth academy. Both brothers are the first cousin of professional golfer [[Robert MacIntyre]].

'''Hamzad Sayeed Kargbo''' (born 20 January 2002) is an English [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a striker for {{English football updater|Stenhous}} club [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hamzad Kargbo {{!}} Football Stats {{!}} Maidstone United {{!}} Age 24 {{!}} Soccer Base |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=144282 |access-date=2026-07-04 |website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref>

==Career==
===Queens Park Rangers===
Kargbo joined the [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] academy aged twelve from Elite Mass Academy, progressing through the ranks to sign a scholarship in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.qpr.co.uk/news/under-18s-news/qpr-youngsters-sign-scholarships|title=QPR youngsters sign scholarships|website=www.qpr.co.uk|date=2 July 2018|accessdate=12 September 2024}}</ref>

In August 2021, Kargbo joined [[National League (division)|National League]] side [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]] on loan until the end of September 2021,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.qpr.co.uk/news/club-news/hamzad-kargbo-joins-southend-on-loan-180821/|title=Hamzad Kargbo joins Southend on loan|website=www.qpr.co.uk|date=18 August 2021|accessdate=12 September 2024}}</ref> later extended for a further month.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.qpr.co.uk/news/club-news/kargbo-southend-loan-extended-011021/|title=Kargbo's Southend loan extended|website=www.qpr.co.uk|date=1 October 2021|accessdate=12 September 2024}}</ref>

In March 2022, Kargbo joined [[National League South]] club [[Oxford City F.C.|Oxford City]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oxfordcityfc.co.uk/oxford-city-confirm-hamzad-kargbo-loan|title=Oxford City confirm Hamzad Kargbo loan|website=www.oxfordcityfc.co.uk|date=24 March 2022|accessdate=12 September 2024}}</ref>

Following the conclusion of the [[2023–24 Queens Park Rangers F.C. season|2023–24 season]], Kargbo was confirmed to be among those leaving the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.qpr.co.uk/news/2024/may/13/development-squad-departures/|title=Development Squad departures|website=www.qpr.co.uk|date=13 May 2024|accessdate=12 September 2024}}</ref>

===Newport County===
In June 2024, Kargbo joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]] following a successful trial period.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c0k4jlzvk7jo|title=Hamzad Kargbo: Striker joins Newport County after trial|date=August 8, 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 10 August 2024, he made his debut in the 2024–25 season opening day 3–2 defeat to [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]] as an 85th minute substitute,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cjdk5ky8zj9t?page=2|title=Cheltenham Town 3-2 Newport County|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> suffering a dislocated shoulder that would require surgery and rule him out for an estimated period of three months.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cm2397100vvo|title=Newport County: New striker Hamzad Kargbo faces time out with shoulder injury|date=August 13, 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.southwalesargus.co.uk/sport/24522159.newport-county-striker-hamzad-kargbo-shoulder-op/|title=Newport County striker Hamzad Kargbo to have shoulder op|publisher=South Wales Argus|last=Kirwan|first=Chris|date=16 August 2024|accessdate=12 September 2024}}</ref>

On 20 January 2025, Kargbo joined [[National League South]] club [[Chippenham Town F.C.|Chippenham Town]] for the remainder of the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/ckgye1873r9o|title=Newport County: Striker Hamzad Kargbo joins Chippenham on loan|website=BBC Sport|date=20 January 2025|accessdate=12 April 2025}}</ref> On 18 March, he returned to his parent club after suffering an injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chippenhamtown.com/hamzad-kargbo-returns-to-newport-county/|title=Hamzad Kargbo returns to Newport County|website=Chippenham Town F.C.|date=18 March 2025|accessdate=12 April 2025}}</ref>  He was released by Newport County at the end of the 2024-25 season.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cev4ew3zn70o Kargbo released by Newport]</ref>

===Maidstone United===
In September 2025, Kargbo joined National League South club [[Maidstone United F.C.|Maidstone United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://maidstoneunited.co.uk/09/19/two-new-ahead-of-this-weekends-match/|title=Two new ahead of this weekend's match|website=maidstoneunited.co.uk|date=19 September 2025|accessdate=21 September 2025}}</ref>

=== Inverness Caledonian Thistle ===
After a successful trial period, where he scored on his first outing in a friendly vs [[Nairn County F.C.|Nairn County]], Kargbo signed a one year deal with [[Scottish Championship]] side, [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on 4 July 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-04 |title=Caley Jags sign striker ahead of Highland League derby |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-jags-sign-striker-ahead-of-highland-league-derby-439243/ |access-date=2026-07-04 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref> However, on 4 September 2026, Kargbo terminated his contract by mutual consent.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-04 |title=Striker leaves Inverness Caledonian Thistle just 62 days after signing for the club |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/striker-leaves-inverness-caledonian-thistle-just-62-days-aft-444142/ |access-date=2026-09-04 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

===Stenhousemuir===
On 5 September 2026, having signed for the club the previous day and appeared as a substitute that evening in a 1–0 victory over [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], Scottish Championship club [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] officially announced the signing of Kargbo.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/2026/09/05/hamzad-kargbo-is-a-warrior/|title=Hamzad Kargbo Is A Warrior|website=www.stenhousemuirfc.com|date=5 September 2026|accessdate=5 September 2026}}</ref>

He began his career as a youth with [[Hamilton Academical F.C. Reserves and Academy|Hamilton Academical]], before joining [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] in 2023. He was subsequently loaned out to [[Lincoln United F.C.|Lincoln United]] and [[Hereford F.C.|Hereford]], before returning to Scotland on a permanent deal with [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].
